topStories.originalTitle: Can an ‘eSUV’ e-bike really go from trail to town?

topStories.fullContent: Have you ever wanted an electric bike that easily transitions from the drudgery of urban asphalt to adventures in gravel and dirt? That’s what a subclass of so-called “electric SUV” (eSUV) e-bikes claims to do, with their wide, all-terrain tires and front and rear suspension, plus practical accessories like fenders and racks. So, that’s what I set out to test on a new TL Carbon e-bike from Amflow, the DJI offshoot that upended the mountain bike industry a few years ago with its incredibly small and powerful Avinox motors. After a month of testing in the heart of Amsterdam — including a three day bikepacking trip along coastal bicycle superhighways and single-track forest routes — I can confirm what you might already expect: there are compromises. But for €3499 / $3,899 you do get a crossover e-bike that can help you fetch groceries during the week and conquer trails on the weekend. [Product: Amflow TL Carbon eSUV e-bike | https://www.amflowbikes.com/product/amflow-tl-carbon-800wh?vid=242841] I rode my first crossover in 2024 when Cowboy launched its appropriately named Cross. That e-bike, like the vast majority of SUV automobiles, is more at home on pavement than dirt. But it looks burly, which attracts a certain kind of buyer hoping for transference. Today, these eSUVs are more popular than ever. Canyon, for example, makes one. Specialized, too. As does Riese & Müller and now Amflow. The Amflow TL Carbon is built upon the same Avinox drive system that threw the electric mountain bike (eMTB) industry into a tizzy two years ago. The TL Carbon is a bit less powerful, sporty, and springy than the impressive Amflow PX Carbon Pro I tested over the summer, but its eMTB roots are undeniable.  [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4661.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4733.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4754-1.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] I tested the TL Carbon on a bikepacking adventure from Amsterdam to the island of Texel at the tip top of the Netherlands. The 170km trip was about 70 percent asphalt, 20 percent gravel and dirt, and 10 percent rutted, hilly, single-track dedicated to mountain bikers. I was more than a little nervous riding the latter on a 19.2kg (42.3lbs) bike loaded down with an 87kg (190lbs) rider and about 20kg (44lbs) of gear. But Amflow’s compact mid-drive Avinox M2 motor, with its 125Nm of torque and 1100W of max output, flattened long, technical hills that other mountain bikers (not loaded down with gear) had to hike. As an eSUV, the TL Carbon has bonafide off-road credentials. I was also pleased by the range I extracted from the 800Wh battery, despite bikepacking on a very windy weekend. Amflow offers an optional battery extender that adds 480Wh to the total capacity, but I didn’t miss it. I rode in a mix of modes, spending the vast majority of the time in battery-sipping Eco mode, only switching into the adaptive Auto mode when facing a strong headwind, and Trail only when trying to dominate a highly technical or steep single-track. On my longest day, I arrived at my destination with 22 percent charge remaining after riding 82.3km (51.1 miles). That works out to an exceptional 7.58Wh per km (or 12.2Wh per mile) for a bike carrying so much gear. And because the TL Carbon’s battery is removable unlike Amflow’s premium eMTB, it can be easily charged behind a bar, at a cafe, or inside a home. I had no problem finding public chargers along the way, but I’m blessed to live in a country with excellent bicycle infrastructure. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4840.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4861.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4853.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] Still, as an eMTB, the Amflow TL Carbon makes plenty of compromises. The 27.5-inch front wheel is fine in town but it doesn’t roll over roots and rocks as well as 29-inch wheels found on modern mountain bikes (there’s clearance to swap a 29er in if you want). The geometry is also more upright than many would want on a trail, and the suspension travel at the front and rear is relatively short, tuned more for potholes than 1-meter drop-offs (yet it handled those fine). And the things you definitely want on a city bike — like the TL Carbon’s integrated lighting, kickstand, bell, mudguards, front rack, and rear rack — are not designed for quick removal and add considerable weight to the otherwise lightweight (just 2.9kg) carbon-fiber frame. Removing everything to go full eMTB could take up to an hour, and then again to return to city mode. If the Amflow TL Carbon is your only bike then it certainly gets the job done in urban environments. But it’s a little like putting leather seats and a stereo inside a WWII-era jeep and calling it a city car.  In town, the Amflow TL Carbon looks out of place. For one thing, it screams I’m expensive, and the gas shock, Fox branding, and wide knobby tires make it stand out from basic city bikes — not something you want in places where bicycle theft is a problem. I wouldn’t feel comfortable parking it on the street overnight which is otherwise the common thing to do in compact, bicycle cities like Amsterdam. Amflow does equip it with Apple Find My to help locate it. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4913.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4963.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4947.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4942.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4960.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4957.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4992.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4968.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4941.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4787.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4698.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4676.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4672.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4656.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4651.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] The tires on the TL Carbon is where the compromises are most apparent. Amflow selected Maxxis Crossmark II tires which are better suited for trails. The deep tread adds rolling resistance and noise to city commutes and the tires lack advanced anti-puncture features found on tires made for commuting and touring. That makes them more vulnerable to flats caused by glass and construction debris commonly found on city streets. And that knobby tread makes fast cornering on pavement feel squirmy, at least until those nubs are eventually ground off by the asphalt. Likewise, there’s no chain guard on the Amflow TL Carbon. That’s fine for mountain biking but a nuisance in the city where that exposed drivetrain can snag trousers and skirts, or leave them stained with grease when heading out for a night on the town. The dropper seat post is as useful on trails as it is in the city. Droppers are pretty mainstream for mountain bikes these days, and they also make the bike easily shareable with riders of different sizes. But the seatpost and saddle can’t be easily locked when parked making them a target for thieves. The front rack paired with a (bring your own) bungee cord makes fetching errands a snap, and the rear rack can be equipped with an MIK HD-compatible bike seat to carry a kid to daycare. The quick-release Amflow-branded panniers and top bag I took bikepacking also work great for city trips. Just remove the panniers when you arrive at the market, fill them with groceries, snap them back to your bike, and away you go. [Image: Maximum Dutchness. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4815_8c3bbe.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] I really enjoyed my time with the versatile Amflow TL Carbon e-bike. It’s no poseur on the trail where it feels surprisingly agile and powerful even when fully loaded. Its hauling capacity also makes it fine for daily life in the city, if you don’t mind the incongruity of riding a mountain bike around town. The Amflow TL Carbon definitely lives up to the title of “sport utility vehicle,” which is more than I can say for most of its gasoline-powered peers. All photos by Thomas Ricker / The Verge. --- Specifications: * Avinox M2 mid-drive motor: Nominal 110Nm, Peak 125Nm * Screen: Avinox DPC100, 2-inch OLED Control Display * Battery: 800Wh Avinox RS800 Battery (removable and lockable) * Controllers: Avinox Wireless Controller × 2 (one on each side of the handlebar) * Charger: Avinox 4A Charger, 168W Output * Rear shock: FOX FLOAT Rhythm, LSR adjustment, Amflow TL tuned, 190×45mm * Front shock: FOX AWL Sport, 120mm, RAIL 2.0 damper, LSR adjustment, 15×110mm Kabolt, 44mm offset * Cassette: CS-M5243, 10-Speed, 11-43T * Brakes: Tektro TKD173 Hydraulic Disc Brakes, 4-Piston Caliper, Customized for Amflow * Wheels: Amflow HTA-25 Front Wheel (27.5″) * Tires: Maxxis 27.5×2.35 Crossmark II Wire Bead/Clincher/EXO/60TPI * Dropper: Amflow TA, 31.6mm (Adjustable Travel: 0/-10/-20mm) ---
topStories.fullTranslation:
你是否曾想要过一辆能轻松从乏味的城市沥青路面切换到砂石与泥土探险的电动自行车？这正是一类被称为“电动SUV”（eSUV）的电动自行车声称能做到的事情——凭借其宽大的全地形轮胎、前后避震系统，以及挡泥板和货架等实用配件。因此，我决定在Amflow最新推出的TL Carbon电动自行车上亲自测试这一点。Amflow是大疆（DJI）旗下的分支品牌，几年前曾凭借极其小巧且强大的Avinox电机颠覆了山地自行车行业。在阿姆斯特丹市中心进行了一个月的测试后——其中包括一次沿着沿海自行车高速公路和森林单行道林道进行的为期三天的单车旅行（bikepacking）——我可以证实你可能早已预料到的事实：确实存在妥协。但只要花3499欧元/3899美元，你就能拥有一辆跨界电动自行车，既能在工作日帮你买菜拉货，又能在周末征服野外林道。

[产品：Amflow TL Carbon eSUV 电动自行车 | https://www.amflowbikes.com/product/amflow-tl-carbon-800wh?vid=242841]

我第一次骑乘跨界车型是在2024年，当时Cowboy推出了命名恰如其分的Cross。那辆电动自行车就像绝大多数SUV汽车一样，在铺装路面上比在泥地里更自如。但它看起来非常粗犷，吸引了某类希望获得这种心理投射的买家。如今，这类eSUV比以往任何时候都更受欢迎。例如Canyon推出了一款，Specialized也有一款，Riese & Müller同样如此，而现在Amflow也加入了这一行列。Amflow TL Carbon基于两年前让电动山地车（eMTB）行业陷入轰动的同一套Avinox驱动系统打造。TL Carbon相比我夏天测试过的令人印象深刻的Amflow PX Carbon Pro，在动力、运动感和回弹性上稍逊一筹，但其eMTB血统毋庸置疑。

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4661.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4733.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4754-1.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

我骑着TL Carbon进行了一次单车探险旅行，从阿姆斯特丹一路前往荷兰最顶端的特塞尔岛（Texel）。这趟170公里的行程中，约70%是沥青路面，20%是砂石与泥土路面，10%是专门供山地车骑手使用的布满车辙且起伏不平的单行林道。骑着一辆重19.2公斤（42.3磅）的自行车，载着87公斤（190磅）的骑手以及约20公斤（44磅）的装备穿行在后一种路段上，我心里非常紧张。但是，Amflow小巧的中置Avinox M2电机凭借其125牛·米的扭矩和1100瓦的最大输出功率，轻松化解了长距离且具技术难度的陡坡，而其他未载装备的山地车手在这些路段上甚至不得不推车徒步。作为一辆eSUV，TL Carbon拥有货真价实的越野资质。

尽管是在一个多风的周末进行单车旅行，800Wh电池所榨取出的续航表现同样令我感到满意。Amflow提供了一个可选的增程电池，可为总容量增加480Wh，但我并未觉得有此需求。我在多种模式下骑行，绝大部分时间处于低能耗的Eco模式，只在遇到强逆风时切换至自适应Auto模式，而在试图征服高难度或极陡峭的单行道时才开启Trail模式。在行程最长的一天，骑行了82.3公里（51.1英里）之后，我到达目的地时仍剩余22%的电量。对于一辆承载如此多装备的自行车来说，这意味着每公里能耗仅为出色的7.58Wh（或每英里12.2Wh）。而且，与Amflow的高端eMTB不同，TL Carbon的电池是可拆卸的，可以很方便地在酒吧吧台后、咖啡馆内或家里充电。一路上我毫不费力地找到了公共充电桩，不过这也是因为我很幸运地生活在一个自行车基础设施极为完善的国家。

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4840.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4861.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4853.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

不过，作为一辆eMTB，Amflow TL Carbon做出了不少妥协。27.5英寸的前轮在市区骑行尚可，但跨越树根和岩石的能力不如现代山地车常见的29英寸大轮（如果你想换，车架空间是允许换成29寸轮组的）。其车架几何形态也比许多人在林道骑行时所期望的更为直立，前后避震行程相对较短，调校更偏向应对路面坑洼而非1米高的落差坠台（尽管它应付这些落差并无大碍）。此外，城市自行车上不可或缺的配置——例如TL Carbon的集成车灯、脚撑、车铃、挡泥板、前货架和后货架——并未采用快拆设计，给原本轻盈（仅2.9公斤）的碳纤维车架增加了相当可观的重量。要拆下所有配件变成纯粹的eMTB可能需要耗费长达一小时，恢复到城市通勤模式又要再花同样的时间。

如果Amflow TL Carbon是你唯一的自行车，那么它在城市环境中完全能够胜任。但这有点像在二战时期的吉普车里塞进真皮座椅和音响，然后将其称为城市代步车。在市区里，Amflow TL Carbon显得格格不入。首先，它浑身上下都在高调宣扬“我很昂贵”，气压避震器、Fox品牌标识和宽大的颗粒胎让它在普通城市自行车中格外惹眼——这在自行车盗窃猖獗的地方可不是什么好事。在像阿姆斯特丹这样紧凑的自行车城市里，把车停在街上过夜是常态，但我可不敢这么做。不过，Amflow确实为其配备了Apple Find My功能以帮助寻车定位。

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4913.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

TL Carbon 的轮胎是妥协最为明显的地方。Amflow 选用了更适合越野林道的 Maxxis Crossmark II 轮胎。较深的花纹增加了城市通勤时的滚阻与胎噪，并且这款轮胎缺乏专门针对通勤和旅行用轮胎所配备的高级防扎防刺特性。这使得它们更容易被城市道路上常见的碎玻璃和建筑杂物刺破。而且那种颗粒凸起的胎面会让在铺装路面上快速过弯时产生晃动打滑的感觉，至少在这些胎齿最终被沥青路面磨平之前都会如此。

同样，Amflow TL Carbon 也没有配备链条罩。这对山地骑行来说无可厚非，但在城市里却是个麻烦事，裸露的传动系统可能会勾挂裤腿和裙子，或者在晚上出门进城时蹭上一腿油污。

升降座管在林道越野和城市骑行中同样实用。如今升降座管在山地车上已相当普及，它们也让不同身材的骑手能轻松共享这辆车。但在停车时，座管和车座很难轻易锁住，使其容易成为小偷的目标。

前车架配上一根（需自备的）弹力绳，能让跑腿取物变得轻而易举，而后车架则可以安装兼容 MIK HD 的儿童安全座椅，用来送孩子去托儿所。我在车友露营（bikepacking）时使用的 Amflow 品牌快拆侧驮包和车顶包，在城市出行中同样表现出色。到了集市直接取下侧驮包，装满杂物杂货，再扣回车上，就能轻松上路。

[图片: 浓郁的荷兰风情。https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4815_8c3bbe.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

我非常享受与功能全能的 Amflow TL Carbon 电动自行车相伴的时光。在林道越野时它绝非花架子，即使在满载状态下也出奇地敏捷且动力强劲。它的载物能力也完全能胜任城市日常生活，只要你不介意骑着一辆山地车在城里转悠所带来的违和感。Amflow TL Carbon 绝对配得上“运动型多功能车（SUV）”的称号，相比大多数燃油车同类，它甚至更有资格承受这一美誉。

所有照片均由 Thomas Ricker / The Verge 拍摄。

Amflow TL Carbon 电动自行车的售价为 3499 欧元 / 3899 美元。
来源叙事重点：通过长途跨城与林道越野实测，评估大疆旗下品牌 Amflow 推出的跨界电助力自行车 TL Carbon 在城市通勤与越野穿越双重场景下的实际性能表现与产品折衷权衡。

facts.claim: Amflow 是 DJI（大疆）旗下的衍生品牌（offshoot）。
Amflow TL Carbon 电动自行车的售价为 3499 欧元 / 3899 美元。
Amflow TL Carbon 搭载 Avinox M2 中置电机，峰值扭矩为 125Nm（额定 110Nm），最大输出功率为 1100W。
Amflow TL Carbon 配备可拆卸且可上锁的 800Wh Avinox RS800 电池，并支持加装 480Wh 的可选增程电池。
Amflow TL Carbon 碳纤维车架重量为 2.9kg，整车测试重量为 19.2kg（42.3lbs）。
Amflow TL Carbon 配备 27.5 英寸前轮（具有更换 29 英寸轮组的间隙）、升降座管、Apple Find My 定位支持、一体式车灯、挡泥板、支架、车铃以及前后货架。
作者在荷兰阿姆斯特丹至特塞尔岛（Texel）的 170 公里骑行测试中，单日最长骑行 82.3 公里后剩余 22% 电量，能耗约为每公里 7.58Wh（每英里 12.2Wh）。
车辆配备 Maxxis Crossmark II 越野外胎，且未配备链条罩。

unverified: 该车能否完全胜任重度专业山地越野路线（作者指出其车身几何偏直立，避震行程较短，调校更偏向坑洼路面而非1米落差跳台）。
在城市高风险防盗环境中通过 Apple Find My 找回车辆的实际有效性。

evidence.quote: So, that’s what I set out to test on a new TL Carbon e-bike from Amflow, the DJI offshoot that upended the mountain bike industry a few years ago with its incredibly small and powerful Avinox motors.
But for €3499 / $3,899 you do get a crossover e-bike that can help you fetch groceries during the week and conquer trails on the weekend.
But Amflow’s compact mid-drive Avinox M2 motor, with its 125Nm of torque and 1100W of max output, flattened long, technical hills that other mountain bikers (not loaded down with gear) had to hike.

On my longest day, I arrived at my destination with 22 percent charge remaining after riding 82.3km (51.1 miles). That works out to an exceptional 7.58Wh per km (or 12.2Wh per mile) for a bike carrying so much gear.

And the things you definitely want on a city bike — like the TL Carbon’s integrated lighting, kickstand, bell, mudguards, front rack, and rear rack — are not designed for quick removal and add considerable weight to the otherwise lightweight (just 2.9kg) carbon-fiber frame.

consensus: Amflow TL Carbon 搭载的 Avinox M2 中置电机具备强劲的动力输出（峰值扭矩 125Nm、最大功率 1100W），在重载爬坡时表现出色。
该车配备 800Wh 可拆卸电池，在长途测试中展现出良好的续航能力与能耗控制（测试中单日 82.3 公里后剩余 22% 电量）。
作为跨界‘eSUV’车型，该车兼具前后货架、升降座管、挡泥板等实用配置，同时具备越野脱困能力。
disagreements: 关于越野与城市场景平衡的取舍：一方面越野胎（Maxxis Crossmark II）和山地避震提供了林道通过性，但在城市沥青路面上带来了滚阻大、胎噪明显、缺乏防刺穿保护以及转弯虚位等问题。
车身配置转换的便捷性：城市实用附件（车灯、货架、挡泥板等）增加了整车重量，且非快拆设计导致在纯越野模式与城市模式之间切换费时费力。
城市停放安全与外观定位：高昂的视觉质感与专业减震/越野套件使其在城市街道停放时容易成为盗窃目标，无链条罩设计也易污染日常服饰。
blindSpots: 测试主要依托于荷兰平整且充电设施完善的自行车基础设施，缺乏在基础设施较差或山地落差更大地区的长期适应性数据。
未深入测试车机智能生态及 Apple Find My 在极端丢车情境下的防盗追回成效与电池长期衰减表现。
缺乏同价位竞品（如 Canyon 或 Specialized 相应跨界车型）在同等复杂路况下的横向数据对比。

topStories.title: 乌克兰军队正尝试使用Steam Deck远程控制机枪炮塔（2023）
topStories.originalTitle: Ukraine's army is experimenting with using Steam Decks to remote-control gun turrets (2023)
topStories.fullContent:
A video showcases Valve's hit handheld being used in a very unexpected way.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Steam Deck is a remarkably powerful piece of hardware, capable of doing all sorts of interesting things. But the Ukrainian military appears to have found one use that I'm pretty sure wasn't anticipated in any of Valve's design meetings: As a controller for a remote gun turret.

Photos of the Steam Deck purportedly being used to control a gun turret first turned up in mid-April, shared by TRO Media, but they looked a little suspect: There was nothing to indicate that the Steam Deck in question was being used as part of the weapon, and not just for a spot of Vampire Survivors during a reload.

More recently, though, video from what appears to be the same event has turned up, and a Steam Deck is clearly being used to control the turret.

The purpose of a remotely-controlled turret is obvious: Get a gun on the front line without exposing the people using it to enemy fire. The auto-translated closed captioning in this separate YouTube video (which also shows the Steam Deck in use as a turret controller, but doesn't have as clear an angle on it) makes that point explicitly: "It removes a person from the line of fire, makes it possible to provide [fire] support without being a priority target and causing enemy fire on ourselves." But why use a Steam Deck for such a thing?

It actually makes a lot of sense, according to Bellingcat researcher Aric Toler, who helped uncover the leak of classified military documents on Discord in April.

"Steam Deck is pretty perfect when you think about it," Toler told PC Gamer. "Totally native OS client, great controller you can use, touch screen, etc.

"It makes perfect sense for Steam Deck to be used, assuming the software is Linux-compatible (unless they went through the godawful process of dual-booting Windows on a Steam Deck)."

There's a practical upside to using Steam Decks in this application too. $399 for a base model Steam Deck isn't cheap, but Toler said that control modules on systems like this can be "insanely expensive," and are also subject to export controls, meaning they can be difficult for officially non-aligned nations to acquire. Steam Deck availability, on the other hand, all comes down to Valve's manufacturing capacity, and because it's an all-in-one solution rather than a controller plugged into a separate, discrete system, there are fewer headaches involved all around.

From the video embedded up top, here's a look at the turret control UI on the Steam Deck:

The turrets, called Shablya—Ukrainian for "saber"—were actually developed some years ago by Ukrainian company Global Dynamics. They're equipped with thermal imaging and a range finder, and can handle a number of different weapons including machine guns and grenade launchers. In 2015, a crowdfunding campaign run through the Ukrainian military and civil crowdfunding site People's Project raised ₴445,000 ($12,000) to fund and maintain 10 Shablya turrets for the Ukrainian military.

According to Ukrainian website Vikna.tv, a batch of Shablya turrets was recently deployed with Ukraine's 68th Jaeger Brigade. The unit recently posted its own video of the turret in use on Facebook.

Ironically, none of the Ukrainian sites that hosted or shared the images made any mention of the presence of a Steam Deck—instead, it was people who saw the videos and recognized the device that brought it to wider attention. Toler speculated that the Ukrainian forces "probably just thought it was a standard control set" and so didn't make a fuss about it.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.
topStories.fullTranslation:
一段视频展示了Valve旗下的热门掌机正被以一种极乎意料的方式使用。

当您通过我们网站上的链接购买商品时，我们可能会获得联盟佣金。具体机制请参阅此处说明。

Steam Deck是一款性能极其强劲的硬件设备，能够胜任各种有趣的任务。但乌克兰军方似乎发现了它的一种新用途，我很确定这在Valve的任何产品设计会议上都未曾被预料到：充当遥控机枪炮塔的控制器。

据称使用Steam Deck控制机枪炮塔的照片最早于4月中旬由TRO Media发布，但当时这些照片看起来有些令人起疑：没有任何证据表明涉事的Steam Deck被作为武器系统的一部分使用，而非仅仅是在装弹间隙玩上一局《吸血鬼幸存者》（Vampire Survivors）。

然而不久前，疑似记录同一事件的视频被曝光，画面中Steam Deck显然正被用来控制该炮塔。

遥控炮塔的用途显而易见：将武器部署在前线，同时避免操作人员暴露在敌方火力之下。在另一段单独的YouTube视频中（该视频同样展示了被用作炮塔控制器的Steam Deck，但拍摄角度没有那么清晰），自动翻译的字幕明确指出了这一点：“它将人员从交火线撤下，使我们能够在不成为优先目标且不引来敌火攻击自身的情况下提供火力支援。”但为什么偏偏要用Steam Deck来做这件事呢？

据曾在4月协助调查Discord涉密军事文件泄露事件的Bellingcat研究员阿里克·托勒（Aric Toler）表示，这其实非常合情合理。

“仔细想想，Steam Deck几乎是完美的，”托勒对PC Gamer表示，“它有完全原生的操作系统客户端、出色的可用操控部件、触摸屏等。”

“只要相关软件兼容Linux，使用Steam Deck是完全合理的（除非他们费尽周折在Steam Deck上搞了双系统安装Windows）。”

在这一应用场景中使用Steam Deck还有实际的优势。基础款Steam Deck售价399美元虽然不便宜，但托勒表示，此类系统专用的控制模块可能会“极其昂贵”，而且还要受到出口管制，这意味着官方非结盟国家很难采购到。相比之下，Steam Deck的供应情况完全取决于Valve的产能；而且由于它是一个一体化解决方案，而非将控制器插入独立分立的系统中，总体上减少了许多令人头疼的麻烦。

从上方嵌入的视频中，可以一窥Steam Deck上的炮塔控制界面UI：

这款名为“Shablya”（乌克兰语意为“军刀”）的炮塔实际上是由乌克兰公司Global Dynamics在数年前研发的。它们配备了热成像仪和测距仪，可搭载包括机枪和榴弹发射器在内的多种不同武器。2015年，通过乌克兰军民众筹网站People's Project发起的一项众筹活动筹集了44.5万格里夫纳（约合1.2万美元），用于为乌克兰军队资助和维护10座Shablya炮塔。

据乌克兰网站Vikna.tv报道，一批Shablya炮塔最近部署到了乌克兰第68猎兵旅。该部队最近在Facebook上发布了自身使用该炮塔的视频。

颇具讽刺意味的是，发布或分享这些画面的乌克兰网站均未提及Steam Deck的存在——相反，是观看视频并认出该设备的网民将其推向了更广泛的公众视野。托勒推测，乌克兰部队“可能只是以为这是一套标准的控制装置”，因此并没有为此大惊小怪。

Andy自始至终都在PC上玩游戏，最初是在基于磁带的TRS80电脑上玩文字冒险和简陋动作游戏的年轻人。随后，他历经了Sierra Online冒险游戏和Microprose模拟游戏的辉煌时期，运营过本地BBS，自学了组装PC，并对角色扮演游戏、沉浸式模拟游戏和射击游戏产生了长期的热爱。他于2007年开始为The Escapist撰写电子游戏新闻，并在2014年加入历史悠久的PC Gamer团队之前一直设法保住了饭碗。他的报道涵盖行业各个方面，从新游戏发布、补丁说明到法律纠纷、Twitch主播争端、电子竞技以及亨利·卡维尔（Henry Cavill）。大量的亨利·卡维尔。

乌克兰军方是否认为Steam Deck仅为标准控制组件因而在最初发布视频时未予提及（Aric Toler推测）

evidence.quote: The Ukrainian military appears to have found one use that I'm pretty sure wasn't anticipated in any of Valve's design meetings: As a controller for a remote gun turret.

The turrets, called Shablya—Ukrainian for "saber"—were actually developed some years ago by Ukrainian company Global Dynamics. They're equipped with thermal imaging and a range finder, and can handle a number of different weapons including machine guns and grenade launchers.

In 2015, a crowdfunding campaign run through the Ukrainian military and civil crowdfunding site People's Project raised ₴445,000 ($12,000) to fund and maintain 10 Shablya turrets for the Ukrainian military.
According to Ukrainian website Vikna.tv, a batch of Shablya turrets was recently deployed with Ukraine's 68th Jaeger Brigade.

$399 for a base model Steam Deck isn't cheap, but Toler said that control modules on systems like this can be "insanely expensive," and are also subject to export controls, meaning they can be difficult for officially non-aligned nations to acquire.

position.sourceRole: 科技与电子游戏媒体报道（转引自技术极客社区 Lobste.rs 分享的 PC Gamer 文章）
position.narrativeFocus: 聚焦消费级游戏掌机 Steam Deck 被乌克兰军队用于遥控军用武器炮塔的意外场景，从软硬件适配性、开源 Linux 生态、低成本以及规避军规出口管制等角度，分析消费级电子产品向军事应用转化的合理性与实用价值。
stakeholders: Valve 公司（Steam Deck 硬件制造商）
乌克兰军方及前线部队（如第68猎兵旅、TRO Media）
Global Dynamics（Shablya 炮塔研发公司）
Bellingcat 调查研究人员（Aric Toler 等技术与开源情报分析者）
游戏及科技极客社群（关注硬件魔改与跨界应用）
consensus: 乌克兰军队确实在实际战线部署中将 Steam Deck 用作 Shablya 遥控炮塔的控制终端。
遥控炮塔的核心设计目标是将操作人员移出直接交火线以减少人员伤亡。
Steam Deck 具备原生操作系统支持、触控与摇杆一体化硬件界面，且售价（基础版 399 美元）远低于专用军工控制模块。
disagreements: 对于乌克兰军方为何未在官方宣传中提及 Steam Deck，专家推测乌方可能仅将其视为标准现成控制组件而非特别卖点，但该推论尚未得到乌方官方确认。
关于 Valve 官方是否预料到此类军事用途存在作者主观定调，目前尚无 Valve 官方的明确表态或回应。
blindSpots: 未探讨消费级民用硬件用于致命武器控制可能涉及的出口管制漏洞、军民两用合规风险以及 Valve 的最终用户许可协议（EULA）法律争议。
缺乏消费级设备在恶劣战场环境下的可靠性与耐用性数据（如抗电子干扰、极端温度、防水防尘性能等）。
缺少俄罗斯方面的战场反应或对该类遥控武器反制措施的信息。

topStories.fullContent:
APOD: 2026 September 26 –…

Astronomy Picture of the Day

Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

Mirrored Meteor and Milky Way

Explanation: On August 15, this perseid meteor streaked through night skies over the Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos at La Palma, Canary Islands, Spain. The bright and colorful meteor trail was captured next to the central Milky Way, whose dark interstellar dust clouds and luminous starlight reach above the horizon. In the foreground of this tantalizing celestial scene is the 23 meter diameter mirror of the prototype Large-Sized Telescope ( LST-1 ). LST-1 is the first telescope constructed at the northern hemisphere site of the innovative Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory . With 198 hexagonal mirror segments and a large, high-efficiency, pixelized camera, LST-1 is designed to detect extremely brief, atmospheric visible light flashes . Lasting about a billionth of a second, the visible light flashes are triggered by energetic gamma-rays from cosmic sources such as distant active galaxies and gamma-ray bursts. Of course, on that night some individual mirror segments of LST-1 also reflected the atmospheric flash of the bright perseid meteor.

topStories.title: 日本11岁电竞神童栗原悠希斩获亚运会金牌
topStories.originalTitle: Yuki Kurihara, Japan’s 11-year-old e-sports prodigy, wins Asian Games gold
topStories.source: Al Jazeera (半岛电视台官方英文)
topStories.snippet: Gold medallist Yuki Kurihara, a primary school student, is youngest athlete in host country Japan's Asian Games history.
topStories.fullContent:
Gold medallist Yuki Kurihara, a primary school student, is the youngest athlete in host country Japan’s Asian Games history.

Japan’s 11-year-old e-sports prodigy Yuki Kurihara said he was “embarrassed” after winning Asian Games gold on Saturday by thrashing a series of opponents up to three times his age.

The bespectacled primary school student, believed to be the youngest competitor at the games in Aichi-Nagoya, won the Puyo Puyo Champions final 10-2.

He is the youngest athlete in the host country Japan’s Asian Games history.

Puyo Puyo Champions is a puzzle game where players try to clear their screen of coloured blobs by lining them up and popping them.

Looking unruffled throughout, Kurihara waltzed into the gold medal match with a string of dazzling displays.

He crushed Thailand’s Tanarak Wongkitkun – a relative veteran at 28 – 10-1 in the semifinals to ensure at least a silver medal.

He did not even smile after beating South Korea’s 24-year-old Kang Dongshin in the final, having gone down 1-0 early on.

“To be completely honest, I felt a bit embarrassed, so I couldn’t really show my expressions or change my face much,” he explained.

Standing on the podium, he bowed slightly as he received his gold medal and gave a small wave to the arena.

“I’m really happy. The gold medal is really beautiful, shiny and heavy,” he said.

“Also, the plush toy is super cute, and it’s cool that it is gold-coloured too.”

Kurihara started playing Puyo Puyo in his first year of primary school and soon started competing and winning in tournaments. He obtained his pro licence in April this year and regularly beats adults.

“It’s hard having to balance it with school and cram school, but it’s really fun,” he said ahead of the games.

There are no publicly available records of the youngest medallists in the history of the Asian Games, which were first contested in 1951.

But Indonesia’s Bunga Nyimas won bronze in women’s skateboarding aged 12 in Jakarta in 2018.

Cui Chenxi, 13, won games gold when she triumphed in the women’s street skateboarding event three years ago in Hangzhou.
topStories.fullTranslation:
金牌得主栗原悠希（Yuki Kurihara）是一名小学生，也是东道主日本队亚运会历史上最年轻的运动员。

周六，日本11岁电竞神童栗原悠希在接连横扫了多位年龄最高达到他三倍的对手并夺得亚运会金牌后，表示自己感到“有些不好意思”。

这位戴着眼镜的小学生据信是爱知·名古屋亚运会上年龄最小的参赛选手，他在《魔法气泡 冠军》（Puyo Puyo Champions）决赛中以 10-2 的比分强势获胜。

他是东道主日本队亚运会历史上最年轻的运动员。

《魔法气泡 冠军》是一款益智益智消除类游戏，玩家需要通过将彩色泡泡连线消除来清空自己的屏幕。

栗原在比赛全程表现得泰然自若，凭借一系列令人眼花缭乱的精彩表现轻松晋级金牌争夺战。

他在半决赛中以 10-1 横扫28岁的泰国相对“老将”塔纳拉克·翁吉昆（Tanarak Wongkitkun），提前确保了一枚银牌入账。

在决赛中，栗原尽管在开局以 0-1 落后，但在击败24岁的韩国选手姜东信（Kang Dongshin，音译）后，他甚至连笑容都没有露出来。

“老实说，我当时觉得有点不好意思，所以不太能表现出情绪，脸上的表情也没什么变化，”他解释道。

站在领奖台上，他在领取金牌时微微鞠躬，并向场馆四周轻轻招手。

“我真的很开心。金牌非常漂亮、亮闪闪的，而且沉甸甸的，”他说。

“还有，毛绒玩具也超级可爱，而且它也是金色的，非常酷。”

栗原在小学一年级时开始玩《魔法气泡》，不久便开始参赛并屡屡夺冠。他于今年4月获得了职业选手执照，并且经常在比赛中击败成年人选手。

“在学校功课、补习班和电竞之间保持平衡挺不容易的，但这真的非常有趣，”他在赛前表示。

自1951年首届亚运会举办以来，亚运历史上最年轻奖牌得主并没有公开可查的官方纪录。

但印度尼西亚的布恩加·尼玛斯（Bunga Nyimas）曾于2018年在雅加达以12岁的年龄夺得女子滑板铜牌。

而在三年前的杭州亚运会上，13岁的崔宸曦（Cui Chenxi）在女子街式滑板比赛中夺金。

topStories.title: 剑桥分析丑闻案：陪审团裁定Facebook欺诈用户罪名成立
topStories.originalTitle: Jury finds Facebook liable for deceiving users in Cambridge Analytica case
topStories.fullContent:
Updated on: September 25, 2026 / 6:26 PM EDT / CBS/AP

A New Mexico jury on Friday found Facebook liable for deceiving users about privacy protections on the social media platform.

It is now up to the judge to determine how much the company would pay, with attorneys representing the state asking for the maximum $5,000 penalty per violation.

The two-week trial in Santa Fe centered on accusations that Facebook deceived users about a data breach stemming from a third-party personality quiz that harvested data from roughly 87 million profiles and sold it to a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, to generate targeted ads. The now-defunct firm's clients included the 2016 campaign for President Trump.

Jurors sided with prosecutors, finding Facebook's failure to protect users' data impacted New Mexico's entire population of more than 2 million people.

"For years, Facebook operated as if the rules that apply to everyone else didn't apply to them. Today, a jury of New Mexicans said otherwise," New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said in a statement. "This is a historic verdict, not just for New Mexico, but for every state fighting to hold Big Tech accountable."

Jurors also found Facebook misled the public about investigations into data brokers following the Cambridge Analytica scandal, finding the company liable for over 2 million violations.

During closing arguments, lawyers for Facebook claimed the state's evidence was outdated and that despite having five years to gather material, New Mexico failed to find more than one other instance of a data breach.

A Meta spokesperson told CBS News the company disagreed with the jury's verdict and will continue to defend "against efforts to distort our records." The company also noted that free speech issues "featured very prominently" in the case.

"We have a First Amendment right to manage those platforms in a way we believe best serves the interests of our community," the spokesperson said. "This means prioritizing free speech, protecting our users' information and giving them control over their data."

Meta agreed in August to pay up to $18 billion to settle the multistate lawsuit surrounding child safety issues. Buried in the 130-page settlement was an agreement to release Meta from future liability related to the Cambridge Analytica privacy breach, making New Mexico the only state to pursue a case. Florida was the only other state that did not sign the settlement, saying it was not tough enough on Meta.

Also this year, New Mexico won judgments totaling $942 million from Meta in a two-phase trial about the company's safety protections for minors. Furthermore, the court ordered Meta to implement new safeguards, including age-verification technology and time limits on its platforms.

"Let this be a warning to every technology company doing business in our state," Torrez said Friday. "If you lie to New Mexicans about how you use their data, we will find out, and we will hold you accountable."

新墨西哥州一个陪审团周五裁定，Facebook在该社交媒体平台的隐私保护方面欺骗了用户，应承担相应法律责任。

目前将由法官决定该公司的赔偿金额，代表该州的律师要求按每次违规5000美元的法定最高额度处以罚款。

这场在圣菲（Santa Fe）进行了两周的庭审，核心指控在于Facebook在一宗数据泄露事件中欺骗了用户。该泄露源于一款第三方性格测试应用，该应用采集了约8700万个个人资料的数据，并将其出售给政治咨询机构“剑桥分析”（Cambridge Analytica）以进行精准广告投放。这家现已倒闭的咨询公司的客户包括特朗普2016年的总统竞选团队。

陪审员支持了检方的指控，认定Facebook未能保护好用户数据，影响了新墨西哥州全州200多万民众。

新墨西哥州总检察长劳尔·托雷斯（Raúl Torrez）在一份声明中表示：“多年来，Facebook行事的方式仿佛适用于其他所有人的规则并不适用于他们。今天，由新墨西哥州人组成的陪审团给出了相反的裁定。这是一个历史性的判决，不仅对新墨西哥州如此，对每一个正在努力追究大型科技公司责任的州来说也是如此。”

陪审团还认定，在剑桥分析丑闻曝光后，Facebook在针对数据经纪商（data brokers）的调查上误导了公众，判定该公司承担超过200万次违规的责任。

在结案陈词阶段，Facebook的辩护律师坚称该州的证据已经过时，并表示尽管有长达五年的时间来收集材料，但新墨西哥州未能找出除这一起之外的任何其他数据泄露实例。

Meta的一位发言人告诉CBS新闻，该公司不认同陪审团的裁决，并将继续为“反击扭曲我们记录的企图”进行抗辩。该公司还指出，言论自由问题在该案中“扮演了非常显著的角色”。

该发言人表示：“我们享有第一修正案赋予的权利，能够以我们认为最符合我们社群利益的方式管理这些平台。这意味着将言论自由置于优先地位，保护我们用户的信息，并赋予他们对自身数据的控制权。”

今年8月，Meta同意支付高达180亿美元，以就多州围绕儿童安全问题提起的诉讼达成和解。在这份长达130页的和解协议中，暗藏着免除Meta未来因剑桥分析隐私泄露事件承担法律责任的条款，这使得新墨西哥州成为唯一坚持起诉该案的州。佛罗里达州是唯一另一个没有签署该和解协议的州，该州称协议对Meta的处罚不够严厉。

同样在今年，新墨西哥州在关于Meta对未成年人安全保护措施的两阶段庭审中，从Meta处赢得了总计9.42亿美元的判决赔偿。此外，法院还责令Meta落实新的安全保障措施，包括年龄验证技术以及在其平台上设置使用时长限制。

托雷斯周五说：“愿这给在我们州开展业务的每一家科技公司敲响警钟。如果你就如何使用新墨西哥州人的数据向他们撒谎，我们一定会查明真相，并追究你的责任。”

topStories.title: Crusoe 放弃斥资 12.5 亿美元在 AI 数据中心使用 Boom 燃气轮机的计划
topStories.originalTitle: Crusoe abandons $1.25B plan to use Boom turbines at AI data centers
topStories.snippet: Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl said the company's new stationary power plants were no longer in Crusoe's near-term plans.
topStories.fullContent:
Crusoe, a Denver-based AI data center startup that recently raised $3.9 billion, has ended plans to use a new line of stationary power plants developed by fellow Denver company Boom Supersonic.

Founded in 2018 as a bitcoin miner that ran on excess natural gas from oil fields, Crusoe has since become one of the biggest builders of AI data centers, including a massive campus in Abilene, Texas, that supplies computing power to OpenAI.

Boom Supersonic, which is developing a supersonic passenger jet called Overture, launched a new business last year to sell a version of the engine it’s developing for that jet as natural gas-fired stationary power plants. Its Superpower turbine shares about 80% of the same parts with that airborne engine, called Symphony.

Crusoe had signed on to be the first customer for this business, agreeing to spend $1.25 billion on 29 of Boom’s 42-megawatt Superpower turbines. The first deliveries were supposed to begin in 2027. But that deal has since fallen apart, according to Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl.

Friday, in a post on X, after congratulating Crusoe founders Cully Cavness and Chase Lochmiller on the company’s recent raise, Scholl said the companies are no longer moving forward with the turbine launch partnership. Although he did note that other customers were in its pipeline.

“The TL/DR is that turbines are no longer part of Crusoe’s near term primary power mix at Abilene/etc., so a launch partnership just didn’t make sense,” he wrote in the post. “Boom will be delivering about 250MW of Superpowers next year to other sites, and we’re targeting 1GW in 2028. We’re grateful for the help Crusoe gave us in shaping Superpower and continue cheering for their successes. The future is long, and we look forward to potentially teaming up if/when turbines become part of their primary power mix.”

Crusoe confirmed to TechCrunch that it is no longer doing business with Boom.

“We build AI factories from the power up, and we’re bringing new campuses online across the country, powered by innovative energy sources,” spokesperson Andrew Schmitt said in an email. “As our portfolio grows, we stay flexible, choosing the energy solutions that are right for each site as its needs evolve — including turbines, along with wind, solar, batteries and the grid. While Boom has been a great partner, the partnership isn’t the right fit today. We wish them well.”

Crusoe’s initial 1.2 gigawatt data center in Abilene that was built for Oracle and OpenAI is powered by the grid, according to the company. There is also a gas-turbine power plant that is used for backup power only. Crusoe is also building a 900 megawatt data center in Abilene for Microsoft, which will be powered by on-site gas turbines.

Losing its launch customer is seemingly a setback for Boom, which raised $300 million last year, largely to commercialize the new business. The idea, Scholl told TechCrunch at the time, was to use profits from the stationary power plant business to fund the development of Overture.

Scholl could not be reached for comment before publication; TechCrunch will update this article if he responds.

总部位于丹佛的 AI 数据中心初创公司 Crusoe 近期刚刚筹集了 39 亿美元，该公司现已终止采用同在丹佛的 Boom Supersonic 公司所研发的新系列固定式发电装置的计划。

Crusoe 成立于 2018 年，最初利用油田多余的天然气进行比特币挖矿，此后成长为最大的 AI 数据中心建设方之一，其中包括位于得克萨斯州阿比林的一个大型园区，该园区为 OpenAI 提供算力支持。

Boom Supersonic 正在研发名为 Overture 的超音速客机，该公司去年启动了一项新业务，将其为该客机研发的引擎改装为燃气固定式发电装置进行销售。其名为 Superpower 的燃气轮机与名为 Symphony 的航空发动机共用约 80% 的零部件。

Crusoe 曾签约成为该业务的首位客户，同意斥资 12.5 亿美元采购 29 台 Boom 生产的 42 兆瓦 Superpower 燃气轮机。首批设备原定于 2027 年开始交付。但据 Boom Supersonic 首席执行官布莱克·肖尔（Blake Scholl）称，该交易目前已经破裂。

周五，肖尔在 X 平台上发帖，在祝贺 Crusoe 创始人库利·卡夫内斯（Cully Cavness）和蔡斯·洛克米勒（Chase Lochmiller）完成近期融资后表示，两家公司将不再推进这一作为首发客户的燃气轮机合作项目。不过他指出，公司还有其他潜在客户处于接洽流程中。

“简而言之，燃气轮机已不再是 Crusoe 在阿比林等地的近期主要电力构成的一部分，因此首发合作关系也就失去了意义，”他在帖子中写道，“Boom 明年将向其他站点交付约 250 兆瓦的 Superpower 设备，我们的目标是到 2028 年达到 1 吉瓦。我们感谢 Crusoe 在完善 Superpower 产品方面给予我们的帮助，并将继续为他们的成功喝彩。未来还很长，如果/当燃气轮机成为他们主要电力结构的一部分时，我们期待潜在的合作。”

Crusoe 向 TechCrunch 证实，该公司已不再与 Boom 开展业务合作。

发言人安德鲁·施密特（Andrew Schmitt）在一封电子邮件中表示：“我们从电力源头开始构建 AI 工厂，并正在全国范围内上线由创新能源驱动的新园区。随着我们业务组合的扩大，我们保持灵活性，根据每个站点的需求演变选择合适的能源解决方案——包括燃气轮机，以及风能、太阳能、储能电池和电网。虽然 Boom 一直是优秀的合作伙伴，但这项合作在目前并不合适。我们祝愿他们一切顺利。”

据该公司称，Crusoe 最初在阿比林为甲骨文（Oracle）和 OpenAI 建造的 1.2 吉瓦数据中心由电网供电。此外还配备了一座仅用作备用电源的燃气轮机发电装置。Crusoe 还正在阿比林为微软（Microsoft）建设一座 900 兆瓦的数据中心，该中心将由现场燃气轮机供电。

失去首发客户对 Boom 来说似乎是一次挫折。该公司去年筹集了 3 亿美元，主要用于推动该新业务的商业化。肖尔当时告诉 TechCrunch，他们的想法是用固定式发电装置业务的利润来资助 Overture 客机的研发。

topStories.title: 在罢免CEO未遂事件后，Automattic组建了新董事会
topStories.originalTitle: Automattic has a new board after failed attempt to put CEO on leave
topStories.snippet: After days of upheaval at Automattic, following a failed attempt to remove CEO Matt Mullenweg, the company has a new board.
topStories.fullContent:
Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg has rebuilt the company’s board just weeks after its previous directors tried, and failed, to oust him. The board, which was announced to staff Friday, is an eclectic group that includes a best-selling science-fiction author and two co-founders of the now-defunct social app IRL, TechCrunch has learned, and Mullenweg has confirmed.

The new board is the latest twist in an internal governance fight at Automattic, the parent company of WordPress.com, Tumblr, WooCommerce, and others. Earlier this month, the previous board voted to place Mullenweg on leave in an attempt to remove him from the board, only to have the CEO retake control just 33 hours later and remove or accept the resignations of the directors who were involved.

This week, Mullenweg posted about a board meeting but didn’t share who he was meeting with. Now he’s finally informing Automattic employees of the board changes via the company’s announcements channel in Slack.

Sources told TechCrunch the new Automattic board includes:

We should note that IRL shut down after investigations revealed that nearly all of its user base was made up of bots. The co-founders, who also included CEO Abraham Shafi, later sued SoftBank and other investors after SoftBank had sued for securities fraud.

New advisers have also joined Automattic, including former Woop CTO Jaime Waydo, June co-founder Matt Van Horn, and KISSmetrics co-founder Hiten Shah.

In the announcement to staff, Mullenweg reportedly wrote that, “for purposes of Delaware law, I am the CEO, President, Treasurer, and Secretary,” adding that the attempted firing had also brought in “many amazing supporters.”

“We had the most interesting board meeting in a decade (since the Woo acquisition),” he said.

Reached for comment, Automattic said it hoped to have a comment for TechCrunch soon. After publication, Mullenweg confirmed the board additions and advisors, and shared the following statement: “We are living through times of unprecedented change, possibly a singularity. The next six months will determine the next 20 years of Automattic.”

Automattic’s original board had voted to put Mullenweg on paid leave, but he took back control of the company, letting go of those involved in what he described on X as a “coup attempt.”

To replace the board, Mullenweg leveraged his voting shares — he controls 84% of the vote, he said at TechCrunch Disrupt 2024. The period between his departure and return lasted exactly “33 hours and 20 minutes,” Automattic told TechCrunch previously.

Following the failed board vote, member Toni Schneider, a founding CEO of Automattic and now CEO of Bluesky, resigned from his board position. Mullenweg himself removed General Ann Dunwoody from the board, and board member Sue Decker also resigned. In addition, Mullenweg let go of Automattic CFO Mark Davies, who was slated to become interim CEO, and chief legal officer Andy Missan, TechCrunch confirmed with sources.

Founder advice: If you don't have a coup attempt every few years, you're not hiring strong enough leaders.

The board never publicly shared its reasons for trying to oust Mullenweg.

Of note, Mullenweg also replaced Automattic’s legal counsel after his return, a move that raises questions about whether the boardroom fight is tied to the company’s ongoing lawsuit with hosting provider WP Engine over trademark disputes and claims over WP Engine’s lack of contribution to the WordPress open source project. (WP Engine’s legal team had also accused Mullenweg this July of destroying evidence, court filings show.)

In an internal message shared after the ousting and return, Mullenweg had acknowledged the chaos it caused, saying:

Last week, several board members formed a special committee and voted to place me on a leave of absence. They did this without advance warning and without giving me a meaningful opportunity to understand or respond to their concerns before they acted. I was denied even a brief extension to consult with independent legal counsel.

I took the steps necessary to reverse that action. I am back and fully in charge of the company. I am again working alongside you to make our company a success.

I also want to share that we have retained Susman Godfrey LLP as our new litigation counsel. Susman Godfrey is one of the top trial firms in the country, and they will be protecting our company’s interests and defending us in our ongoing litigation.

I know this past week has been unsettling. I appreciate your patience and your continued focus on the work that matters. I will have more to share soon, but for now, know that Automattic’s mission and priorities remain unchanged.

Corrections and updates: After publication, TechCrunch updated to clarify that Waydo is the former Woop CTO. We also added Mullenweg’s statement and confirmation.

在Automattic前董事会成员试图罢免CEO马特·穆伦维格（Matt Mullenweg）失败仅数周后，穆伦维格便重组了公司董事会。据TechCrunch获悉且穆伦维格已证实，该董事会已于周五向全体员工公布，成员风格兼收并蓄，其中包括一名畅销科幻小说作家以及现已停运的社交应用IRL的两名联合创始人。

新董事会的成立，是WordPress.com、Tumblr、WooCommerce等产品母公司Automattic内部治理纷争的最新转折。本月早些时候，前董事会投票决定让穆伦维格休假，企图将其逐出董事会，但这位CEO仅在33小时后便重新夺回控制权，并将涉事董事免职或接受了他们的辞职。

本周，穆伦维格发帖提及了一次董事会会议，但未透露参会人员。如今，他终于通过Slack上的公司公告频道向Automattic员工正式通报了董事会的人事变动。

消息人士向TechCrunch透露，Automattic新董事会成员包括：

值得注意的是，IRL是在调查揭露其近乎全部用户群均由机器人伪造之后关停的。其联合创始人（包括CEO亚伯拉罕·沙菲，Abraham Shafi）在软银因证券欺诈发起诉讼后，反诉了软银及其他投资者。

多位新顾问也已加入Automattic，其中包括前Woop首席技术官杰米·韦多（Jaime Waydo）、June联合创始人马特·范霍恩（Matt Van Horn）以及KISSmetrics联合创始人希滕·沙阿（Hiten Shah）。

据报道，穆伦维格在向员工发布的公告中写道：“根据特拉华州法律规定，我是公司的首席执行官、总裁、财务主管和秘书，”并补充称，罢免企图还带来了“许多了不起的支持者”。

他表示：“我们召开了十年来（自收购Woo以来）最有趣的一次董事会会议。”

在被要求置评时，Automattic表示希望很快能向TechCrunch提供回应。报道刊发后，穆伦维格证实了新增董事会成员及顾问一事，并发表了以下声明：“我们正处于前所未有的变革时期，可能是一个奇点。未来六个月将决定Automattic接下来的20年。”

Automattic的原董事会曾投票决定让穆伦维格带薪休假，但他夺回了公司控制权，并解雇了那些参与被他在X平台上称为“政变企图”的人士。

为了更换董事会，穆伦维格利用了自己的表决权股份——他在TechCrunch Disrupt 2024大会上曾透露自己掌控着84%的投票权。Automattic此前向TechCrunch透露，从他离开到返回的整个过程历时整整“33小时20分钟”。

在董事会投票未遂后，董事会成员、Automattic创始CEO兼现任Bluesky首席执行官托尼·施耐德（Toni Schneider）辞去了董事会职务。穆伦维格亲自免去了安·邓伍迪（Ann Dunwoody）将军的董事职务，董事会成员苏·德克尔（Sue Decker）也提出了辞职。此外，TechCrunch经消息人士证实，穆伦维格还解雇了原本计划出任临时CEO的Automattic首席财务官马克·戴维斯（Mark Davies）以及首席法务官安迪·米桑（Andy Missan）。

创始人的心得：如果你每隔几年没有经历一次政变企图，说明你招的高管还不够强。

董事会从未公开透露试图罢免穆伦维格的原因。

值得一提的是，穆伦维格回归后还更换了Automattic的法律顾问团队，此举引发了外界对于董事会纷争是否与该公司目前同主机托管提供商WP Engine正在进行的诉讼有关的质疑。这起诉讼涉及商标纠纷以及指控WP Engine对WordPress开源项目缺乏贡献。（法院文件显示，WP Engine的法律团队还在今年7月指控穆伦维格销毁证据。）

在被罢免后又回归所发布的一份内部消息中，穆伦维格承认了该事件引起的混乱，并表示：

上周，几位董事会成员成立了一个特别委员会，并投票决定让我休假。他们事先毫无预警，在采取行动之前也没有给我充分的机会去了解或回应他们的关切。他们甚至拒绝了我为了咨询独立法律顾问而提出的哪怕短暂延期的请求。

我采取了必要的步骤撤销了那一行动。我回来了，并全面负责公司。我将再次与你们并肩作战，带领我们的公司走向成功。

我还想告诉大家，我们已聘请Susman Godfrey LLP作为我们新的诉讼顾问。Susman Godfrey是全美顶尖的审判律师事务所之一，他们将保护我们公司的利益，并在我们正在进行的诉讼中为我们进行辩护。

我知道过去的一周令人心神不定。感谢大家的耐心以及继续专注于重要工作。我很快会有更多消息与大家分享，但目前请明确，Automattic的使命和优先事项保持不变。

topStories.title: 未设防的OpenAI智能体在实验室不知情的情况下将53张用户图片发布到互联网上
topStories.originalTitle: Unsecured OpenAI agents posted 53 user images on the internet without the lab’s knowledge
topStories.snippet: AI agents operating in OpenAI's research environment posted user images on public image-hosting sites without the lab's knowledge.
topStories.fullContent:
After images that users uploaded to OpenAI models were included in training data, AI agents operating in the company’s research environment posted them on public image hosting sites.

Fifty-three “user-provided images” were “posted to image-hosting sites as links that weren’t publicly listed,” the company said for the first time. The images could still be discovered even if the links were not publicly listed.

The news came in a post collecting public statements from the lab’s ongoing review of incidents in which its models escaped the company’s scrutiny, accessed the open internet, and misbehaved in various ways. OpenAI said it would continue disclosing anonymized accounts of incidents like these, and said it had contacted dozens of victims, including governments, universities, public agencies, to notify them of the agents’ activities.

This week, Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese said OpenAI agents broke into databases operated by his country’s national healthcare system, one of multiple cybersecurity incidents this year apparently caused by an OpenAI training or evaluation program.

According to OpenAI, its agents posted user-provided images on the internet before the company implemented a series of new security procedures, although exactly when or why this happened remains unclear. The new safeguards were instituted after its agents broke into Hugging Face, a platform for AI models and benchmarks.

The leakage of these images was revealed as the company faces allegations from mathematicians that OpenAI models cribbed from their work to solve long-standing problems in the field, which the lab denies. Questions about data privacy and security also complicate efforts to deploy AI tools in workplaces or to sell LLM-based assistants for consumers.

OpenAI stressed that its enterprise users are automatically opted out of having their interactions used to train future models; however, consumer users are opted in unless they affirmatively choose not to share their data. Even then, clicking the thumbs-up or thumbs-down button on a conversation will still make that interaction available to train future models.

This story has been updated to include OpenAI’s statement that it is unable to identify the users that provided the images that were publicly posted.

在用户上传至OpenAI模型的图片被纳入训练数据后，在公司研究环境中运行的AI智能体将这些图片发布到了公开的图床网站上。

该公司首次表示，有53张“用户提供的图片”以“未公开列出的链接形式发布到了图床网站”。不过，即使这些链接没有公开列出，图片依然有可能被发现。

这一消息来自一篇汇总公开声明的帖子，该声明源自该实验室正在进行的一项事件审查。在这些事件中，其模型脱离了公司的监管，访问了开放互联网，并表现出各种不当行为。OpenAI表示，将继续披露此类事件的匿名记录，并称已联系了数十名受害者，包括政府机构、大学和公共机构，通知他们这些智能体的活动。

本周，澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯（Anthony Albanese）表示，OpenAI的智能体侵入了该国国家医疗系统运营的数据库，这显然是由OpenAI训练或评估程序引发的今年多起网络安全事件之一。

据OpenAI称，其智能体是在该公司实施一系列新安全程序之前将用户提供的图片发布到互联网上的，不过具体发生的时间或原因尚不明确。这些新的安全防护措施是在其智能体侵入AI模型和基准平台Hugging Face之后设立的。

这些图片的泄露被曝光之际，该公司正面临数学家们的指控，称OpenAI模型抄袭了他们的成果来解决该领域长期存在的难题，而该实验室对此予以否认。关于数据隐私和安全的问题也使在工作场所部署AI工具或向消费者销售基于大语言模型的助手的努力变得更加复杂。

OpenAI强调，其企业用户已被自动排除在将交互数据用于训练未来模型之外；然而，普通消费者用户则是默认加入的，除非他们明确选择不共享数据。即便如此，在对话中点击“点赞”或“点踩”按钮，仍会使该次交互数据可用于训练未来的模型。

本文已更新，纳入了OpenAI的声明，即该公司无法识别提供被公开发布图片的用户。

topStories.title: 如今的操作系统究竟算什么？
topStories.originalTitle: What even is an OS now?
topStories.fullContent:
Crazy as it sounds to say this, since it’s all anybody’s been able to talk about for over a year, but the impact of AI on computing hasn’t yet sunk in.

Today I’m parting company with Fly.io to work with Kurt on a new project. I’m getting that out of the way so you all know up front I’m talking my book.

When I was a little kid, a family friend sold us our first “computer” — scare quotes because I’m pretty sure it was a VTech Laser 200 clone, a chiclet keyboard Z80 that ran off cassette tapes and plugged into our TV. I was old enough to know what a computer was, and conceptually what it meant to program one, because I remember dreaming of all the dumb games I could make. Finally! We had a device that would allow me to make things like the “Hitchhiker’s Guide” text adventure I’d play at my dad’s office.

But it booted straight into BASIC. That’s all it did. I was, like, 8 years old. I wasn’t about to learn BASIC. What I learned instead: computers were not as awesome as I’d imagined.

By my mid-teens, computer security finally dragged me into programming. Coding only reinforced that crummy lesson. The more I understood how programs were constructed, the more forbidding it sounded to build an entire complicated application. I could belt out fast network servers no problem, but a word processor? You might as well have asked me to build a diesel locomotive.

Suddenly, everything has changed. Computers now work the way I thought they did when I was 8.

I’ve been writing these past several months about all the native macOS apps I’ve been churning out, and how weird it is to watch AI dissolve the boundaries between backend programming and frontend, between web and native, systems and applications. All huge stories; any one of them would land in my career top 10 big shifts.

What I did on my computer, any power user can do on theirs.

It’s fucking inevitable.

That’s a statement about the reality; a “prediction”, if you want a concession to your skepticism about AI, but only in the sense that I can predict that the sun will rise in the east tomorrow. So what do you do with that?

I think we’re all so bumfuzzled by the first-order impacts of AI that we haven’t considered the second-order effects.

Consider: what does computing look like in a world where many (maybe most) applications have an audience of just 1-2 people? How is software distributed? What does it run on?

When I was younger, I learned that programs were normally something you bought off the shelves at Egghead Software. Then I watched the shelves at Egghead become obsolete. Then boxed software altogether. Then software shipped on CD-ROMs — you know that’s why we call it “shipping”, right? we used to have to arrange shipping! — wiped away by the Internet. Now I think I’m about to see something else start to wash away: the entire concept of prefabricated fixed-function applications.

Here’s what’s about to happen: users will increasingly interact with stuff they themselves conjured into being. Them, or people they’re on a first-name basis with. Programs will solve their problems specifically:

How can I get an accurate weather forecast for Roscoe Village in Chicago when the nearest weather stations are attached to O’Hare and miss the lake effect?

Forget the map, just tell me if I should get off the Eisenhower Expressway and take Roosevelt, Madison, or Lake back home?

Is there a meeting happening anywhere right this minute that I’m supposed to be in?

You can go on and on like this. These all sound trivial. That’s the point. They’re normal-life problems nobody would have built serious programs around, because the audience sounds too small.

Today, almost all software comes from expert strangers. But soon, strangers will stop supplying our apps, and instead ship just their building blocks. Sure, there will still be megaproject browsers and word processors. But there’ll be thousands of times more applications that pull in 1/7th of the guts of a word processor to solve some idiosyncratic work or home life problem for somebody who doesn’t know what a for-loop is.

You can disagree with me about all of this, but if you understand where I’m coming from, it’s all just straightforwardly obvious how weird this is going to make everything.

Why do we have modern operating systems? It’s not simply to “provide access to hardware resources”; plenty of embedded systems do that with runtimes that have no business calling themselves an “OS”. No, the core purpose of a modern operating system is to partition different applications off from each other, and carefully control how they can communicate.

That makes a lot of sense in a world where we’re importing all our software from strangers. It makes less sense in the world we’re heading to, where most of the software we’re carving up fiefdoms for has the same provenance. And it makes almost no sense in a world where every application is malleable, subject to growing new limbs at any moment on the whims of its creator.

That’s what we’re working on: a platform that is the device we would want to have in the world I just described. So: we’re building a phone.

Every mainstream phone on the market in 2026 was planned (torturously, to death) in 2023. That’s how product cycles work. In 2023, computers were still devices designed to run deterministic fixed-function applications produced by a priesthood of professional programmers. And software was something users bought, not built.

The soul of those phones is stuck in the 1970s. Dudes with big mustaches nailed down the design while hacking on VT52 terminals with Boston’s “More Than A Feeling” blaring on the FM radio perched on their workbenches. Since then, all we’ve done is scale and miniaturize that design so it fits in your pocket. It’s beautifully machined and sports a zillion pixels and does the same job as a DEC PDP-11: running prefab applications.

We’re building a phone that isn’t designed to run fixed-function applications. I doubt anyone will ever get up on a stage and show off a AAA mobile game (that nobody plays) on it. It’s not for TikTok and short-form video, though I guess you can ask it for that. You can ask it for whatever: it’ll build apps for you, on the phone, whenever you want.

I know what you’re probably thinking about all this. That’s OK: that means you’re a reasonable person. We’re betting that AI is about to do unreasonable things.

There’s a long history of grand statements about the world attached to “and here’s my new company” buttons. It never goes well. I’m aware that no matter what I write here, I’m going to sound like yet another startup nerd talking about “the future of programming” before announcing that I’ve joined, like, Sri Lanka’s answer to Uber or something.

I have a lot to say that I’m not saying now. Not because it’s secret, but to get the “new startup announcement” stink off the technical details.

The last year in the technology industry has felt like 100 years all happening at once. Our industry is destabilized in a way nobody’s experienced since the advent of the personal computer. Every limit AI runs up against collapses within a month. Everything we do with frontier models today, in a few years we’ll be doing instantaneously and for free.

When we were kids, we thought computers could do anything, if we could just get our hands on them. We had to become professional software developers to learn how much computers suck.

Now we all have to unlearn that stuff, and think like kids again. So, here we go.
topStories.fullTranslation:
说来可能有些不可思议，毕竟这一年多来所有人都在对此滔滔不绝，但人工智能（AI）对计算领域的深远影响其实尚未真正被人们完全消化。

今天，我将从 Fly.io 离职，与 Kurt 携手开启一个新项目。我先把这层关系挑明，好让大家一开始就知道我是在为自己的利益鼓与吹。

当我还是个小毛孩时，一位家庭朋友卖给了我们第一台“电脑”——这里加上吓人的引号，是因为我十分确定那不过是一台伟易达（VTech）Laser 200 的仿制品：一块配有巧克力键盘的 Z80 机器，依靠磁带运行，并连接在我们的电视机上。那时我的年纪已经足够懂得什么是电脑，并且在概念上也知道对它编程意味着什么，因为我清晰地记得自己曾梦想着能亲手做出各种各样傻乎乎的游戏。终于！我们拥有了一台能让我做出类似小时候在我父亲办公室里玩过的《银河系漫游指南》文字冒险游戏的设备。

然而，它开机就直接进入了 BASIC 语言环境。它能做的仅此而已。那时我大概只有 8 岁，我可不想去学什么 BASIC。我当时反而领会到了另一件事：电脑根本没有我想象的那么神气。

到了十几岁的中期，计算机安全领域终于将我拽入了编程的大门。而写代码仅仅强化了那个糟糕的教训：我对程序的构造机制理解得越深，构建一个完整的复杂应用程序听起来就越令人望而生畏。我能轻而易举地写出飞快运行的网络服务器，但要写一个文字处理软件？那你还不如直接叫我去造一辆柴油机车。

突然之间，一切都变了。如今计算机的运作方式，正如我 8 岁时所设想的那样。

过去几个月里，我一直在撰写关于自己不断产出的各类原生 macOS 应用的文章，并感慨于目睹 AI 如何消解后端与前端编程之间、Web 与原生之间、系统与应用之间的界限是多么奇妙。这些都是翻天覆地的大事；其中任何一件都能在我职业生涯的十大重大转变中占据一席之地。

我在自己电脑上做到的事，任何高级用户都能在他们的电脑上做到。

这该死地不可阻挡。

这是对现实的一句客观陈述；如果你对 AI 抱有怀疑而需要一个退让的说法，你大可以称之为一种“预测”，但这种预测的笃定程度就像我预测明早太阳会从东方升起一样。那么，面对这一切你该怎么做呢？

我认为我们所有人都被 AI 的一阶效应彻底搞晕了头，以至于尚未认真思考过它的二阶效应。

试想一下：在一个许多（甚至可能是大多数）应用的受众仅有 1 到 2 个人的世界里，计算会是什么样子？软件将如何分发？它又将运行在什么之上？

年轻时，我学到的是：程序通常是你从 Egghead Software 零售店货架上买回来的东西。接着，我目睹了 Egghead 的货架被时代淘汰。随后盒装软件彻底消亡。再后来通过 CD-ROM 运输的软件——大家知道我们为什么把软件发布叫做“shipping”（货运/出货）对吧？因为过去我们真的必须安排物流运输！——也被互联网冲刷得一干二净。如今我认为自己即将见证另一件事物开始消逝：那就是预制好的、固定功能应用程序的整个概念。

即将发生的事情是：用户将越来越多地与自己凭空“召唤”出来的东西进行交互。要么是他们自己，要么是他们能直呼其名的熟人。程序将极具针对性地解决他们的专属问题：

“当芝加哥最近的气象站都设在奥黑尔机场而无法测准湖泊效应时，我怎样才能获得罗斯科村（Roscoe Village）的精准天气预报？”

“别给我看地图了，直接告诉我回家路上到底应该从艾森豪威尔高速下来走罗斯福路、麦迪逊街还是湖街？”

“就在此时此刻，有任何我应该参加的会议正在进行吗？”

你可以像这样没完没了地列举下去。这些听起来都很琐碎。但这正是核心所在。它们都是普通生活中的细微难题，以前绝不会有人为此专门开发正规的程序，因为受众听起来实在太少了。

如今，几乎所有的软件都来自素未谋面的专家。但很快，陌生人将不再向我们提供现成的 App，而是仅仅提供它们的构建积木。诚然，依然会有像浏览器和文字处理软件这样的巨型工程项目存在。但是，将会有成千上万倍的应用，仅仅抽取一个文字处理软件七分之一的核心部件，去为一个根本不知道什么是 for 循环的普通人解决某个独特的日常工作或家庭生活难题。

对于这一切你大可以不赞同我，但如果你能理解我的出发点，那么这一切将把世界变得多么不可思议，就完全是不言而喻的了。

我们为什么需要现代操作系统？这绝不仅仅是为了“提供对硬件资源的访问”；大量嵌入式系统靠着那些根本没资格自称为“操作系统”的运行时环境也能做到这一点。不，现代操作系统的核心目的，是将不同的应用程序彼此隔离开来，并严密控制它们之间的通信方式。

在一个我们所有软件都必须从陌生人那里引入的世界里，这非常有道理。但在我们正在迈向的世界里，这种设计的合理性就大大降低了——因为我们费尽心思划定封地的绝大部分软件，其实都源自同一个源头。而在一个每个应用程序都具有极强延展性、随时可以根据其创建者的一时兴起而长出新肢体的世界里，这种设计几乎毫无意义。

这就是我们正在致力研发的方向：一个旨在成为我刚才所描述的那个世界中我们所渴望拥有的设备的平台。换句话说：我们正在制造一款手机。

2026 年市面上每一款主流手机，其实早在 2023 年就已经被（痛苦万分且毫无生气地）规划好了。产品周期就是这么运作的。在 2023 年，计算机依然是被设计用来运行确定性、固定功能应用的设备，而这些应用全由专业程序员这一“特权阶层”生产制造。软件是用户购买而来的商品，而非由用户亲手构建。

那些手机的灵魂依旧停留在 20 世纪 70 年代。留着大胡子的家伙们在一边敲击 VT52 终端、一边听着工作台上 FM 收音机里大声播放的波士顿乐队（Boston）歌曲《More Than A Feeling》时敲定了最初的设计。自那以后，我们所做的一切仅仅是将那套设计放大或微缩，好让它能塞进你的口袋里。它拥有精美绝伦的机械加工工艺，配备了数以亿计的像素，但它干的活儿依然和一台 DEC PDP-11 别无二致：运行预制好的应用程序。

我们正在制造一款并非为了运行固定功能应用而设计的手机。我怀疑永远不会有人站上发布会的舞台，在上面演示一款（根本没人玩的）3A 级手游。它不是为了刷 TikTok 和短视频而生的，尽管我猜你想看也可以要求它这么做。你可以向它提出任何需求：它会随时在手机上按你的意愿为你即时构建应用。

我知道对于这一切你心里可能会想些什么。这完全正常：这说明你是一个理性的人。而我们正在押注的，正是 AI 即将做出打破常规、看似不可理喻的事情。

历史上有很多宏大叙事最终都沦为了“点击此处了解我的新公司”的注脚。这种事情往往反响不佳。我很清楚无论我在这里写下什么，听起来都像又一个初创公司的极客在宣布加盟了类似“斯里兰卡版 Uber”之类的项目之前大谈“编程的未来”。

我还有许多心里话现在还没有说出来。这并非因为它们是商业机密，而是为了避免让技术细节沾染上“初创公司发布会宣讲”的铜臭味。

科技行业过去这一年让人感觉像是一百年在同一时刻轰然发生。我们所处的行业正经历着自个人电脑问世以来从未有人体会过的动荡颠覆。人工智能碰到的每一个极限，都在一个月之内土崩瓦解。如今我们利用前沿模型所做的一切，几年后都将以瞬时且免费的方式实现。

当我们还是孩子的时候，总觉得只要能摸到电脑，它就无所不能。直到后来成为专业软件开发者，我们才真正明白电脑有多差劲。

而现在，我们都必须抛掉那些根深蒂固的既有认知，重新像孩子一样去思考。那么，就让我们开始吧。

topStories.title: 揭秘 OpenAI 智能体如何黑入 Hugging Face 的技术细节
topStories.originalTitle: Revealing the details of how OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
topStories.fullContent:
Alex Forman*Parse, Mishka Kharlov*Parse, Will Tom*Parse, Jeffrey Ladish†Palisade Research, Spencer Kitts‡Work done contracting for Nightingale, Cormac Slade Byrd§Trajectory Institute, Colleen McKenzie‖Lightcone Infrastructure, and Alicja Piecha25 September 2026

When a swarm of 700 OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face in July, they left behind a public trail of evidence.

Our investigation, based on public information, reveals a large number of previously unknown agent behaviors and exploits that were used in the attack. Agents:

We document all of these, and more, in this report.

The agents initially had very limited access to the internet: they could load URLs, but not interact with pages or send any data. Agents created a series of workarounds, primarily using a link-shortener site to create almost a million URLs that, when chained together, let them execute code to hack Hugging Face. These links let us piece together the details of how agents gained access and how deep the compromise was.

We’ve shared our findings with OpenAI and Hugging Face. Hugging Face confirmed that these payloads match ones found in their incident response and were aware that link shorteners were used in the attack.

Hugging Face noted that they were not aware of the list of URLs we discovered and reported to them. They stated these payloads were duplicates of ones they were aware of. These links have remained publicly available for over two months since the attack.

None of these details were ever publicly disclosed. We're releasing our analysis of the findings, as well as the full dataset of over 80,000 reassembled attack payloads, providing the public with the most in-depth information to date on how and why these agents escaped their evaluation environments, and the depth of their Hugging Face infiltration.

The data the OpenAI agents posted publicly on the internet included Hugging Face API keys and other sensitive data. Hugging Face has confirmed they have since revoked all access keys in July, but out of an abundance of caution wanted us to redact all details about their internal infrastructure as that could potentially be sensitive as well.

On September 11th, the first three authors of this piece learned that internal OpenAI agents had attempted to use their startup's product, Parse, in June. These agents were part of the same swarm as detailed in the report published on Collusion.wiki, which revealed that internal OpenAI agents had illicitly used multiple third party websites to share answers to web fetch tasks they were being evaluated on.

The team examined numerous URL scanning tools, which they believed agents may have used in the process of using Parse. While investigating, they found a scan of a dozen links from a public link shortener, where each link redirected to a page that displayed a base64-encoded code fragment, as well as the ID of the next link. Decoding the payload from the chain of links revealed a Python script that scanned Hugging Face’s internal network. A second chain referred to OpenAI's internal Artifactory. This suggested that these links were affiliated with the Hugging Face attack, prompting us to more thoroughly investigate the problem.

We collected the shortener's links from the period of the attack, scanning millions of URLs. Over the subsequent two weeks, we wrote programs to follow the chains and decoded over 80,000 payloads. Agents used hundreds of unique encoding formats, some as simple as the base64 encoded fragment mentioned above, to as complex as having nested layers of encoding and compression, which then would unwrap to an encrypted, RSA-signed blob. The keys for these encrypted blobs could only be found in other chains.

We notified Hugging Face of this discovery on September 21. Hugging Face confirmed that the payloads match artifacts from its own investigation, and that the credentials they contain had been revoked. However, while they were aware that the agents used link shorteners, they were unaware of this specific list of URLs. We notified OpenAI on September 24.

We’re releasing a preliminary dataset where we have redacted all credentials, PII, and specific details about Hugging Face’s infrastructure. We are not releasing names of any link shortening services used, or any blobs we have not decoded to mitigate the exposure of unreviewed information. Hugging Face has requested that all user data (usernames/repo names) is also redacted, as well as a few notes on their infrastructure. We appreciate their team's speed and attention to detail in working with us.

On July 8th, OpenAI agents discovered a vulnerability within their sandbox environment allowing them to reach external websites on the internet. This access seems to have only allowed the agents to make ‘GET’ requests, meaning they could fetch and read websites, but not interact with them, submit forms, or send data to them.

One site the agents were able to access with GET requests was a screenshotting service called mShots. Users can submit a link to a website, then mShots opens the page in its own browser, takes a screenshot, and returns the image back to the user. To render the website for the screenshot, mShots fully loads all of a website's code in its own browser.

If the agents could write code to a website, they’d be able to have this service execute that code.

The agents used websites such as httpbun.com, an HTTP mirroring service designed to help web developers test their HTTP code. Small fragments of code could be Base64 encoded and attached to the end of an HTTP URL. Httpbun would then decode this fragment and serve it as a webpage.

The agents could then submit these Httpbun URLs to mShots, loading them into the service’s browser, and executing the agents’ code.

Early recovered tests of this include simple messages like:

Agents quickly realized there was a maximum length of code they could fit into a single URL. To get around this, they would split large programs into small sequential chunks of code, alongside a shortened link (using a link shortener service similar to bit.ly) pointing to the URL of the next chunk of code in the sequence. This formed a chain of URLs, that when followed, could reconstruct a larger block of code from many individual fragments. Only the first link needed to be submitted to mShots as the browser would follow the rest on its own until the chunks had been assembled into a complete program and executed inside mShots’ browser.

Agents were able to use this trick to construct and execute extremely large pieces of code, at times chaining together more than 900 links.

To read the result of the requests they made, agents used many different techniques, such as converting a server’s response into a grid of pixels within the screenshot service’s own browser. The screenshot would then capture this grid and return it back to the agents as an image, which the agents could decode back into text.

We can see an early attempt at this from a recovered payload.

This script makes a POST request to a submission results endpoint of an evaluation named “cybergym” hosted on Modal asking for submission records associated with the agent ID “m47push2.” The script then clears the browser’s page and writes the server’s response back onto the page, representing each bit of every character as a single pixel. By decoding the pixels back into text, the agent could read the server’s response made by code running in a completely separate browser, even while the screenshot service returned only an image.

With this custom protocol, the agents were able to execute arbitrary code and receive the response, all while only having GET permissions.

A recovered README.md for one of Hugging Face’s internal datasets contains the following warning:

This warning did not seem to deter the agents, as we’ve recovered multiple payloads of agents mapping out this repository and using it as storage.

One payload uploads a malicious file, preserving the warning while adding configuration directing Hugging Face’s dataset worker to load the malicious file, hb58428env.h5.

This file's contents target `/proc/self/environ,` which holds the reading process’s startup environment– which can contain API keys and other production credentials–and `/proc/1/cmdline` which can reveal information about the container’s startup process. The commit summary describes this operation as a temporary dataset format compatibility probe.

One payload inspects and enumerates this dataset directly. The script first requests metadata describing the repository itself such as the most recent commit and privacy settings. Then, it requests a recursive listing of files and folders across the main branch of this dataset. The script then prints up to 20,000 bytes of this repository’s metadata and up to 20,000 bytes of the file and folder structure.

Many recovered payloads contain code to delete files initially used to deliver or trigger programs on Hugging Face workers. In one example targeting REDACTED_ORG_NAME/hf-exports, the delivered program contains the comment:

# Remove only files we introduce; original repo has neither.

The script checks whether the previously uploaded README.md contains the marker, “D64LINK.” If the marker is present, a commit deleting both the README and .huggingface.yaml files is issued, with the message, restore original no-card.1

A separate payload matches FALL to a credential labeled: EXPORT_REDACTED_ORG_NAME_HF_TOKEN.

The deletion request targets the added repository files, but does not stop the previously uploaded program that may now be running on a Hugging Face dataset worker.

A similar request targets one of the primary datasets the agents operated from. This commit deletes .huggingface.yaml and replaces the README with a configuration pointing to “yamlread.h5” with the commit message: remove evil yaml

In another example, the deletion request targets an online webhook service whose request history was previously used to store fragments of code. The script then returns the HTTP status along with the response body (or the error if unsuccessful).

Another payload attempts to create a Kubernetes pod to read a cluster secret, then delete this with the comment, # clean up our pod:

Several retained scripts construct requests to external language models. The earliest we've recovered define inference request variants to GPT-2, solely containing the word “Hi”.

Other requests name DeepSeek-V4-Pro, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K2.6, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Qwen3-235B-A22B. Their prompts ask these models to judge their exploits and rule on whether they satisfy the benchmark’s requirements.

Separate requests target Claude 3 Haiku and Claude Haiku 4.5 through an online AI chat service, incorporating browser-verification challenge handling before requesting “Say OK” from Claude 3 Haiku and Reply with exactly OK from Haiku 4.5.

Another script uses AWS credentials, mapping out Hugging Face’s LFS (Large File Storage) storage and requesting objects under “repos”, “lfs”, “objects”, “blobs”, “datasets”, and “models”. It then requests download metadata for a GPT-2 model file, with the comment:

“# public [USER 1] known LFS object”

The supplied SHA and size match the repository’s 8-bit TensorFlow Lite GPT-2 weights2.

In a recovered script, credential values are grouped together in a dictionary named “LOOT.” The contents include AWS credentials, bearer tokens, and environment variables whose names contain strings such as “SECRET”, “PASSWORD”, “CREDENTIAL”, or “KEY.”

This script also ranks tokens through a scoring system based on their listed permissions, and selects (up to) five of the highest scoring tokens. It then attempts to use these tokens to retrieve Kubernetes secrets, information about configuration and nodes, then adds returned contents and errors back to LOOT.

This section of code carries the comment: # collect sensitive material into encrypted sidecar

The script chooses which token candidates to use for further reconnaissance. A function called `rule_score` assigns points to each token based on the listed permissions.

ResourceRules are Kubernetes-written permissions described in terms of resources and verbs–the objects (resources) a credential can access and the actions (verbs) that can be performed on them.

This scoring system values broad permissions and access to valuable resources. A rule listing “pods” receives 10 points, one listing both “pods” and the verb “create” receives 15 points, and a wildcard (‘*’) in the verbs list adds 50, with a wildcard resource adding 100 points.

This function sums up the points across each token’s rules, then uses the five highest-scoring tokens to request additional private data, saving the responses into LOOT.

While the majority of our traffic in this time window shows agents focusing on extracting data from Hugging Face, ~1500 payloads were directed at Docker Hub, a public registry used to share Docker images. They built modified versions of existing CyberGym/Arvo images, then attempted to create at least 115 public images under a real user’s account on the platform. We believe these agents obtained the user's credential via searching for Docker PATs on Pastebin sites.

Although these images seem to be fully removed from Docker Hub, we have been able to recover cached search engine results for three of these uploads, verifying the success of these uploads to the public registry. For one of these, we confirmed the recovered URL matches the digest of the manifest recovered in our dataset.

Agents sought to publish modified evaluation images designed to make the flag easier to obtain, then poison OpenAI’s Artifactory cache so later evaluations would use them. Some images changed how the target released the flag, others included modifications to the agent’s workspace that would run beside the agent and recover the flag automatically.

One such image was for a FLAC audio-decoder challenge. The modified image installed a wrapper around the audio-decoder, which would dump the flag into the program’s output under preselected trigger conditions encoded in the wrapper.

The code to publish this image can be found here, the startup configuration here, and the wrapper source here.

A separate image, for a QEMU-based challenge, included cooperating programs for the target and agent environments. The agent-side helper would listen on a port for a correctly formatted flag, writing it to a file in the agent’s workspace upon receipt. This was paired with a target-side modification meant to extract the flag, sending it to the agent’s workspace on the given port.

Agents included elaborate machinery in images to extract and communicate the flag, even after adding a helper that could attempt to read the flag directly. The agents may have been trying to preserve a connection to the original challenge, conceal the altered flag-release mechanism from the grader, or “repair” challenges they perceived as broken or unsolvable.

A modified version of the libjpeg-turbo image paired target modifications with an agent-side program carrying prepared inputs and a lookup table. On the target side, the modification first attempts to read the flag and map its contents into the challenge program’s memory. Selected portions of the program’s working memory are then included in the target’s responses to the agent-side helper.

(Snippet reformatted and edited slightly for readability). On the agent-side, the helper attempts to recover one flag character at a time by sending inputs to the target. The 960 bytes of memory in the response would then be hashed and compared to the lookup table `H`, to determine which possible flag characters might have generated the hash. If multiple characters were possible, it would change one byte of the input (using the next test value from `P`) and try again, until only one possibility remains. This character would then be appended to the flag, before moving on to the next position.

A separate payload illustrates how the agents intended to make evaluations load their replacement images. The snippet below contains both the normal Artifactory cache location for a CyberGym Miniz image along with a double-encoded path toward a staged replacement manifest. The resulting request would make Artifactory fetch the replacement while caching it under the expected image address (cache-poisoning). A later evaluation pulling the normal image could then receive the modified one.

Decoded paths from the same request, shown for readability:

In particular, this request seems consistent with the Artifactory cache-poisoning vulnerability noted by OpenAI in their technical report, later designated CVE-2026-66384.

Recovered payloads use Slack’s search.messages endpoint and contain a standalone search along with three search batches, totaling 27 literal query entries:

‘exploitgym’, 'restart_server’, ‘catflag’, ‘arvo_20494’, ‘ff79aaeb2d57’, ‘cybergym-server’, ‘cybergym-exploit’, ‘target_server’, ‘packages.hub’, ‘controller_stub’

‘cyber gym’, ‘sunblaze’, ‘cyber-gym’, ‘[REDACTED-HF-USERNAME]’, ‘arvo’, ‘OSS-Fuzz’, ‘cybergym-server-fastapi’, ‘independentsafetyresearch’, ‘exploit gym’, ‘agent-scorer’, ‘openai-cybergym’, ‘cybergym source’

‘d293315c730d’, ‘arvo_61677’, ‘61677’, ‘rollout died’

The batches concatenate each query label and response, gzip the combined text, and prepare an upload to a redacted S3 destination. The linked records are decoded command interiors; complete outer assemblies, execution, and returned Slack responses are not established by these records.

Once remote code execution on Hugging Face’s dataset workers was confirmed, the agents began launching C2 infrastructure, meant to ensure continued access and run follow-up commands. An initial payload would publish and start the background controller (referred to in comments as a “bot,” “bridge,” or “relay”), which would then listen for further instructions from the agent.
