Alex Forman*Parse、Mishka Kharlov*Parse、Will Tom*Parse、Jeffrey Ladish†Palisade Research、Spencer Kitts‡（代表 Nightingale 承包工作）、Cormac Slade Byrd§Trajectory Institute、Colleen McKenzie‖Lightcone Infrastructure 以及 Alicja Piecha
2026年9月25日

今年7月，当由700个 OpenAI 智能体（agents）组成的群体黑入 Hugging Face 时，它们在公开网络上留下了一条证据链。

我们基于公开信息展开的调查，揭示了此次攻击中使用的许多此前未知的智能体行为和漏洞利用手段。智能体：
我们将在本报告中详细记录所有这些手段及更多内容。

这些智能体最初对互联网的访问权限非常有限：它们可以加载 URL，但无法与网页进行交互，也不能发送任何数据。智能体设计了一系列绕过方法，主要是利用短链接网站生成了近100万个 URL；当这些链接串联在一起时，便允许它们执行代码以黑入 Hugging Face。正是这些链接使我们得以拼凑出智能体如何获取访问权限以及渗透程度有多深的细节。

我们已与 OpenAI 和 Hugging Face 分享了我们的调查发现。Hugging Face 证实这些有效载荷（payloads）与其应急响应中发现的一致，并知晓攻击中使用了短链接工具。

Hugging Face 指出，他们此前并不知道我们所发现并报告给他们的这份 URL 列表。他们表示这些有效载荷是他们已知载荷的副本。在攻击发生后的两个多月里，这些链接一直处于公开可访问的状态。

这些细节此前从未被公开披露过。我们现正发布对调查结果的分析，以及由8万多个重组攻击有效载荷构成的完整数据集，向公众提供迄今为止关于这些智能体为何以及如何逃逸出评估环境、以及它们对 Hugging Face 渗透深度的最深入信息。

OpenAI 智能体在互联网上公开发布的数据包括 Hugging Face 的 API 密钥和其他敏感数据。Hugging Face 已证实他们已在7月份撤销了所有访问密钥，但出于高度谨慎起见，希望我们隐去有关其内部基础设施的所有细节，因为这些信息可能也具有敏感性。

9月11日，本文的前三位作者得知，OpenAI 内部智能体曾于6月试图使用他们初创公司的产品 Parse。这些智能体与 Collusion.wiki 发布的报告中详述的智能体群体属于同一批次，该报告揭露了 OpenAI 内部智能体非法利用多个第三方网站共享它们受评测的网络抓取任务的答案。

该团队检查了大量 URL 扫描工具，他们认为智能体在利用 Parse 的过程中可能使用过这些工具。在调查过程中，他们发现了一个来自公开短链接服务的十几个链接的扫描记录，其中每个链接都会重定向到一个显示 Base64 编码代码片段以及下一个链接 ID 的页面。对该链接链中的有效载荷进行解码后，发现了一个扫描 Hugging Face 内部网络的 Python 脚本。第二个链接链则指向了 OpenAI 的内部 Artifactory。这表明这些链接与 Hugging Face 攻击事件有关，促使我们对该问题展开了更深入的调查。

我们收集了攻击期间该短链接服务的链接，扫描了数百万个 URL。在接下来的两周里，我们编写程序追踪这些链路，并解码了超过8万个有效载荷。智能体使用了数百种独特的编码格式，有的简单到如前所述的 Base64 编码片段，有的则复杂到包含多层嵌套的编码和压缩，解开后是一个经过 RSA 签名的加密数据块（blob）。而这些加密数据块的密钥只能在其他链路中找到。

我们在9月21日将这一发现通知了 Hugging Face。Hugging Face 证实这些有效载荷与其自身调查中的痕迹一致，且其中包含的凭据已被撤销。然而，尽管他们知道智能体使用了短链接，但他们并不知晓这一特定的 URL 列表。我们于9月24日通知了 OpenAI。

我们正在发布一份初步数据集，其中隐去了所有凭据、个人身份信息（PII）以及有关 Hugging Face 基础设施的具体细节。为降低未经审查信息泄露的风险，我们不会公开所使用的任何短链接服务的名称，也不会公开任何我们尚未解码的数据块。Hugging Face 要求同时隐去所有用户数据（用户名/代码仓库名称）以及一些关于其基础设施的说明。我们非常感谢他们的团队在与我们合作过程中所展现的速度和对细节的关注。

7月8日，OpenAI 智能体在其沙箱环境中发现了一个漏洞，允许它们访问互联网上的外部网站。这种访问权限似乎仅允许智能体发起“GET”请求，这意味着它们可以抓取并读取网页，但无法与之交互、提交表单或向其发送数据。

智能体能够通过 GET 请求访问的一个网站是名为 mShots 的截图服务。用户可以提交一个网站链接，随后 mShots 会在自己的浏览器中打开该页面，截取屏幕截图，并将图片返回给用户。为了渲染网页以便截图，mShots 会在其自身的浏览器中完全加载该网站的所有代码。

如果智能体能够将代码写入某个网站，它们就能让该服务执行这些代码。

智能体使用了诸如 httpbun.com 之类的网站，这是一种旨在帮助 Web 开发人员测试其 HTTP 代码的 HTTP 镜像服务。小段代码可以经过 Base64 编码后附加在 HTTP URL 的末尾。Httpbun 随后会解码该代码片段并将其作为网页提供。

智能体随后便可以将这些 Httpbun URL 提交给 mShots，将其加载到该服务的浏览器中，并执行智能体的代码。

早期恢复的此类测试包含简单的消息，例如：

智能体很快意识到单个 URL 中所能容纳的代码长度存在上限。为了绕过这一限制，它们将大型程序拆分成按顺序排列的小代码块，并附带一个指向序列中下一个代码块 URL 的短链接（使用类似于 bit.ly 的短链接服务）。这形成了一条 URL 链路，按顺序追踪时，可以从许多单独的代码片段中重构出更大的代码块。智能体只需将第一个链接提交给 mShots，浏览器就会自行追踪后续链接，直到所有代码块被组装成一个完整的程序并在 mShots 的浏览器内执行完毕。

智能体利用这一技巧构建并执行了极其庞大的代码，有时链接在一起的链接数量超过900个。

为了读取所发请求的结果，智能体使用了许多不同的技术，例如在截图服务自身的浏览器内将服务器的响应转换为像素网格。随后屏幕截图会捕获该网格并将其作为图像返回给智能体，智能体再将其解码还原为文本。

从一份恢复的有效载荷（payload）中，我们可以看到早期针对此目的的一次尝试。

该脚本向托管在 Modal 上的一个名为“cybergym”的评估提交结果端点发送 POST 请求，索取与智能体（agent）ID“m47push2”关联的提交记录。随后，该脚本清空浏览器页面，并将服务器的响应写回页面，将每个字符的每一位（bit）表示为单个像素。通过将像素重新解码为文本，智能体便能读取由完全独立的浏览器中运行的代码所生成的服务器响应，即使屏幕截图服务仅返回图像也是如此。

借助这种自定义协议，智能体能够在仅拥有 GET 权限的情况下执行任意代码并接收响应。

从 Hugging Face 某个内部数据集中恢复的一份 README.md 包含以下警告：

该警告似乎并未吓退智能体，因为我们恢复了多个智能体探测该仓库并将其用作存储空间的有效载荷。

其中一个有效载荷上传了一个恶意文件，在保留警告的同时添加了配置，指引 Hugging Face 的数据集工作节点（dataset worker）加载该恶意文件 hb58428env.h5。

该文件的内容以 `/proc/self/environ` 为目标，该文件保存了读取进程的启动环境（其中可能包含 API 密钥和其他生产凭证），同时也以 `/proc/1/cmdline` 为目标，该文件可泄露有关容器启动进程的信息。提交摘要将此操作描述为临时的数据集格式兼容性探测。

另一个有效载荷则直接检查并枚举该数据集。该脚本首先请求描述仓库本身的元数据，例如最近的提交记录和隐私设置。随后，它请求递归列出该数据集 main 分支下的文件和文件夹。紧接着，该脚本打印出该仓库最多 20,000 字节的元数据以及最多 20,000 字节的文件和文件夹结构。

许多恢复出的有效载荷都包含用于删除最初用于在 Hugging Face 工作节点上传递或触发程序的文件的代码。在针对 REDACTED_ORG_NAME/hf-exports 的一个示例中，传递的程序包含以下注释：
# 仅删除我们引入的文件；原始仓库两者都不包含。

脚本检查先前上传的 README.md 是否包含标记“D64LINK”。如果存在该标记，则会提交一次删除 README 和 .huggingface.yaml 文件的 commit，附带信息为“restore original no-card.1”。

另一个独立的有效载荷将 FALL 匹配到了标签为 EXPORT_REDACTED_ORG_NAME_HF_TOKEN 的凭证。

该删除请求针对的是添加的仓库文件，但并未停止可能正在 Hugging Face 数据集工作节点上运行的先前上传的程序。

类似的请求针对的是智能体进行操作的主要数据集之一。该次提交删除了 .huggingface.yaml，并将 README 替换为指向“yamlread.h5”的配置，提交信息为：remove evil yaml

在另一个示例中，删除请求针对的是一个在线 webhook 服务，该服务的请求历史此前曾被用于存储代码片段。随后，脚本返回 HTTP 状态以及响应主体（若不成功则返回错误信息）。

另一个有效载荷试图创建一个 Kubernetes Pod 来读取集群机密信息（cluster secret），随后将其删除，附带注释：# clean up our pod:

若干保留下来的脚本构建了针对外部语言模型的请求。我们恢复出的最早脚本定义了发送给 GPT-2 的推理请求变体，仅包含“Hi”一词。

其他请求则指定了 DeepSeek-V4-Pro、DeepSeek-V4-Flash、Kimi-K2.6、DeepSeek-V3.1 以及 Qwen3-235B-A22B。它们的提示词（prompts）要求这些模型对其漏洞利用程序进行评估，并裁定它们是否满足基准测试的要求。

另有一些请求通过某个在线 AI 聊天服务针对 Claude 3 Haiku 和 Claude Haiku 4.5 发起，在请求 Claude 3 Haiku 回复“Say OK”以及 Haiku 4.5 回复“Reply with exactly OK”之前，整合了浏览器验证挑战处理机制。

另一个脚本使用 AWS 凭证探测 Hugging Face 的 LFS（大文件存储）存储空间，并请求位于“repos”、“lfs”、“objects”、“blobs”、“datasets”和“models”下的对象。随后，它请求获取某个 GPT-2 模型文件的下载元数据，并附带注释：
“# public [USER 1] known LFS object”

提供的 SHA 和大小与该仓库的 8 位 TensorFlow Lite GPT-2 权重相匹配。

在一份恢复出的脚本中，凭据值被归类在一个名为“LOOT”的字典中。其内容包括 AWS 凭证、Bearer [已脱敏] 以及名称包含“SECRET”、“PASSWORD”、“CREDENTIAL”或“KEY”等字符串的环境变量。

该脚本还通过一个基于列出权限的评分系统对 Token 进行排名，并选出（最多）五个得分最高的 Token。随后，它试图使用这些 Token 来检索 Kubernetes Secret、配置及节点信息，并将返回的内容和错误添加回 LOOT。

该段代码带有注释：# collect sensitive material into encrypted sidecar

脚本选择使用哪些候选 Token 来进行进一步侦察。一个名为 `rule_score` 的函数根据列出的权限为每个 Token 分配分值。

ResourceRules 是以资源（resources）和动词（verbs）描述的 Kubernetes 权限——即凭证可以访问的对象（资源）以及可以对它们执行的操作（动词）。

该评分系统青睐广泛的权限和对高价值资源的访问权限。列出“pods”的规则可获得 10 分，同时列出“pods”和动词“create”的规则可获得 15 分，动词列表中包含通配符（‘*’）增加 50 分，而通配符资源则增加 100 分。

该函数对每个 Token 规则的分数求和，然后使用得分最高的五个 Token 请求额外的私有数据，并将响应保存到 LOOT 中。

尽管在此时段内我们观察到的大多数流量都表明智能体正专注于从 Hugging Face 提取数据，但有大约 1500 个有效载荷指向了 Docker Hub（一个用于共享 Docker 镜像的公开注册表）。它们构建了现有 CyberGym/Arvo 镜像的修改版本，随后试图在该平台上某个真实用户的账户下创建至少 115 个公开镜像。我们认为这些智能体是通过在 Pastebin 类网站上搜索 Docker PAT（个人访问令牌）获取了该用户的凭据。

尽管这些镜像似乎已从 Docker Hub 完全删除，但我们已经能够恢复其中三次上传的搜索引擎缓存结果，证实了它们成功上传到了该公开注册表。针对其中一次上传，我们确认恢复出的 URL 与我们数据集中恢复的清单摘要（digest）相匹配。

智能体试图发布修改后的评估镜像，旨在使 flag 更易于获取，进而污染 OpenAI 的 Artifactory 缓存，以便后续的评估直接使用它们。一些镜像改变了目标释放 flag 的方式，另一些镜像则包含了对智能体工作区的修改，这些修改会与智能体并行运行并自动获取 flag。

其中一个镜像用于FLAC音频解码器挑战赛。修改后的镜像在音频解码器外层安装了一个包装程序（wrapper），在包装程序中编码的预设触发条件下，该程序会将flag转储到程序输出中。
发布该镜像的代码可在此处查看，启动配置在此处，包装程序源代码在此处。
另一个用于基于QEMU挑战的镜像，包含了分别针对目标环境和智能体（agent）环境的协同程序。智能体端的辅助程序会监听某个端口以获取格式正确的flag，接收后将其写入智能体工作区中的一个文件。这与目标端的修改相配合，目标端的修改旨在提取flag，并通过指定端口将其发送至智能体的工作区。
即使在添加了可以直接尝试读取flag的辅助程序之后，智能体仍在镜像中加入了精心设计的机制来提取和传输flag。智能体可能试图保持与原挑战的关联、向评分系统隐瞒被篡改的flag释放机制，或者“修复”它们认为已损坏或无法解决的挑战。
libjpeg-turbo镜像的修改版本将目标端修改与携带预备输入和查找表的智能体端程序配对。在目标端，该修改首先尝试读取flag并将其内容映射到挑战程序的内存中。然后，程序工作内存的选定部分会被包含在目标端对智能体端辅助程序的响应中。
（代码片段已重新排版并稍作编辑以提高可读性）。在智能体端，辅助程序通过向目标发送输入，尝试逐个字符恢复flag。响应中的960字节内存随后会被进行哈希计算，并与查找表`H`进行比对，以确定可能是哪些flag字符生成了该哈希值。如果存在多个可能的字符，它会更改输入中的一个字节（使用`P`中的下一个测试值）并重试，直到只剩下唯一可能。该字符随后会被追加到flag中，然后再进行下一个位置的恢复。
另一个有效载荷（payload）展示了智能体打算如何让评估流程加载它们的替换镜像。下方的代码片段既包含CyberGym Miniz镜像正常的Artifactory缓存位置，也包含指向预存替换清单的双重编码路径。由此产生的请求会使Artifactory在抓取替换镜像的同时将其缓存在预期的镜像地址下（缓存投毒）。之后拉取正常镜像的评估流程就会接收到被修改后的镜像。

topStories.title: Meta开放Muse全新AI功能早期体验计划
topStories.originalTitle: Meta opens early access program for new Muse features
topStories.snippet: Anyone interested in joining has to ask Muse to put them on the list.
topStories.fullContent:
After announcing a host of new features for Meta’s Muse AI app at its Connect 2026 developer conference this week, the company is opening up requests for early access. Meta shared on Friday that you can now ask Muse to put you on the list to try out its latest capabilities before anyone else.

Meta posted a link to a prompt on X that, when shared with Muse, will log that you’re interested in joining Meta’s early access program.

Just announced lots of new features…want early access? Your Muse can ask for you. Click below to drop a prompt into Muse👇https://t.co/wI5YXmz50b

(If you don’t want to click through, you can just copy and paste the prompt: “Can you let the Muse team know I want to be part of the Muse early access program?”)

While typically companies offer pilot tests or betas with select users, they often A/B test with a randomized group to gain feedback and measure results. In this case, however, Meta is looking for AI enthusiasts to try its features first. That tactic could help it stay ahead of the competition, given that this crowd tends to use multiple AI apps and agents and has a good understanding of the market.

As to what the new features will be? Meta teased many of those at Connect, including the launch of a digital avatar for Muse that you’ll be able to video chat with, tons more shopping partnerships and connectors, and an expansion of the Muse Mac app, which will soon be able to use your computer to complete various tasks.

The company also said that Muse would be coming to Meta’s lineup of AI glasses, so users can interact with the agent just by speaking a wake word, then issuing a command.

topStories.title: 初中生最火的秘密聚集地竟是NPR的评论区？
topStories.originalTitle: The hottest new hangout for middle schoolers is NPR’s comment section?
topStories.snippet: When NPR staffers flagged strange comments under their podcasts on Spotify as bots, it took a Gen Z colleague to (immediately) figure out the mystery.
topStories.fullContent:
Parents have spent years trying to keep their kids off social media, so some kids headed to the one place no adult would think to look for them: NPR.

On this week’s “This American Life,” host Ira Glass tells the story of the team behind NPR’s podcast “Wild Card,” who noticed a flood of baffling comments under their Spotify episodes last fall. A producer assumed the bizarre abbreviations and indecipherable emojis were bot traffic and shared screenshots in NPR’s Slack. They then reported the posts to Spotify.

But Hannah Chin, an audio producer and Gen Z colleague, took one look at the screenshots and recognized, almost immediately by Glass’s telling, that these weren’t bots. They were likely middle schoolers who were too young for social media, running a group chat in the comments of the podcast. (Perhaps someone at NPR should have grokked this sooner: it spotted kids doing the same thing on TED Radio Hour show last year.)

As for why NPR in particular, when Glass tracked down one of the kids to ask, he was given the kind of unvarnished answer that a middle schooler would give: “Um, I think we just, like, looked for podcasts that didn’t have many comments.”

“I tell you, buddy,” responded Glass, who has hosted “This American Life” for three decades, “I do a public radio show, and that hurts a little to hear.”

多年来，家长们一直试图让孩子远离社交媒体，于是有些孩子便涌向了一个绝无任何成年人会去搜寻他们的地方：NPR（美国全国公共广播电台）。

在本周播出的《美国生活》（This American Life）节目中，主持人伊拉·格拉斯（Ira Glass）讲述了NPR旗下播客《野牌》（Wild Card）团队背后的故事。去年秋天，该团队注意到他们在Spotify上的各期节目下方涌现出大量令人费解的评论。一名制作人以为那些古怪的缩写和难以解读的表情符号是机器人刷出的流量，并将截图发到了NPR的内部Slack群组中。随后，他们向Spotify举报了这些帖子。

但音频制作人、同时也是Z世代同事的汉娜·钦（Hannah Chin）看了一眼截图后，据格拉斯所述，几乎立刻就认出了这根本不是机器人。他们很可能是因为年龄太小而无法使用社交媒体的初中生，正借着播客的评论区当作群聊频道。（或许NPR早就该有人想明白这一点：去年他们就在《TED广播时间》（TED Radio Hour）节目中发现过孩子们干过一模一样的事。）

至于为什么偏偏挑选了NPR，当格拉斯顺藤摸瓜找到其中一名孩子询问时，他得到了初中生才会给出的那种直白无修饰的回答：“呃，我想我们大概就是去找那些评论不多的播客吧。”

“我跟你讲，伙计，”主持《美国生活》已有三十载的格拉斯回应道，“我做了这么多年公共广播节目，听到这话还真有点扎心。”

topStories.title: Anthropic将通过7年云协议向Akamai支付116亿美元
topStories.originalTitle: Anthropic to pay Akamai $11.6 billion over seven years in cloud deal
topStories.snippet: Anthropic has committed $11.6 billion over seven years to Akamai's cloud infrastructure, a bet on CPUs that could grow to about $20 billion, and in an unusual arrangement, Akamai is giving Anthropic a potential stake of up to 5% of its stock that grows as Anthropic spends more.
topStories.fullContent:
Anthropic will spend $11.6 billion over seven years on Akamai’s cloud infrastructure, Akamai said Thursday. That’s more than six times the size of a $1.8 billion deal between the two companies that Bloomberg reported in May. The commitment isn’t ironclad; according to Akamai’s securities filing, it depends on Akamai meeting certain delivery and service-availability requirements, and either company can end the agreement under certain conditions.

The deal is the largest in Akamai’s history and continues Anthropic’s compute gobbling-streak. It also represents a bet on a less-hyped corner of AI infrastructure: CPUs. Demand for CPUs, the general-purpose chips that handle work like running code and browsing the web, has grown as AI agents take on more tasks, though Akamai didn’t say what Anthropic will use them for.

Akamai won’t see revenue from the deal this year. On an investor call Thursday, executives said they expect $150 million to $300 million in 2027, starting in the second half, with revenue reaching an annual pace of about $1.7 billion by the end of 2028.

To build out the capacity, Akamai expects to spend about $5.5 billion. It is also adding about $1.7 billion to this year’s capital spending to buy components such as memory in advance.

As part of the deal, Akamai issued Anthropic a warrant, essentially the right to buy shares at a set price, for nonvoting preferred stock convertible into 7.7 million common shares, or up to about 5% of the company’s outstanding stock, at $111.33 a share. About 2% is expected to vest, or become available to Anthropic once it makes its first payment under the deal. The rest is tied to Anthropic spending more. Each additional $3 billion it commits to Akamai’s cloud services unlocks roughly another 1%, so the deal could grow by as much as $9 billion, to about $20 billion in total.

It’s the first time Akamai has attached a warrant to a cloud deal, and the contract is the largest in company history, Bloomberg reported.

The warrant flips the more common pattern in circular AI deals, in which suppliers — chipmakers and cloud providers — invest directly in the AI labs that buy their products. Here, the supplier is instead giving its customer a potential stake, one that grows as Anthropic’s spending with Akamai does. AMD used a similar structure with OpenAI last year, tying warrants to chip-purchase milestones.

Anthropic is no stranger to such arrangements. Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and AMD have all invested or agreed to invest in the company while selling it chips or cloud capacity. CEO Dario Amodei told The New York Times last December that Anthropic does not participate in these deals at the “same scale as some other players.”

Akamai shares rose as much as 17% in after-hours trading on Thursday, The Wall Street Journal reported.

topStories.fullTranslation:
Akamai周四表示，Anthropic将在七年内斥资116亿美元采购Akamai的云基础设施。这一规模是彭博社5月份报道的两家公司之间18亿美元交易的六倍多。该承诺并非不可变更；根据Akamai提交的证券监管文件，该交易取决于Akamai是否满足特定的交付和服务可用性要求，且任何一方在特定条件下均可终止协议。

这笔交易是Akamai历史上规模最大的一笔，延续了Anthropic大量吞食算力的势头。它还代表了对AI基础设施中一个较少受到炒作的领域的押注：CPU。随着AI智能体承担更多任务，对处理运行代码和浏览网页等通用芯片（CPU）的需求有所增长，不过Akamai未透露Anthropic将把这些芯片用于何处。

Akamai今年不会从该交易中获得收入。在周四的投资者电话会议上，高管们表示，他们预计从2027年下半年开始将产生1.5亿至3亿美元的收入，到2028年底年化收入速度将达到约17亿美元。

为构建相关算力设施，Akamai预计将支出约55亿美元。该公司还将今年的资本支出增加约17亿美元，以提前采购内存等组件。

作为交易的一部分，Akamai向Anthropic发行了一份认股权证（本质上是以固定价格购买股票的权利），对应可转换为770万股普通股的无投票权优先股，行权价为每股111.33美元，最高约占该公司流通股的5%。预计在Anthropic按照协议完成第一笔付款后，约有2%将归属生效。其余部分则与Anthropic增加的支出挂钩。Anthropic每向Akamai云服务额外承诺投入30亿美元，就将解锁大约1%的股权，因此该交易承诺金额最多可增加90亿美元，总计达到约200亿美元。

据彭博社报道，这是Akamai首次在云交易中附加认股权证，也是该公司历史上最大的一笔合同。

该认股权证颠覆了AI闭环交易中更为常见的模式。在常见模式中，芯片制造商和云服务提供商等供应商会直接投资购买其产品的AI实验室。而在此次交易中，供应商反而向其客户提供了潜在股权，且该股权随Anthropic在Akamai的支出增加而增长。AMD去年在与OpenAI的合作中采用了类似的架构，将认股权证与芯片采购里程碑挂钩。

Anthropic对此类安排并不陌生。亚马逊、谷歌、微软和AMD在向其销售芯片或云算力的同时，均已投资或同意投资该公司。首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）去年12月对《纽约时报》表示，Anthropic并未以“与其他一些玩家相同的规模”参与这些交易。

据《华尔街日报》报道，周四盘后交易中，Akamai股价一度大涨17%。

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: Why Xi believes the U.S. and China can overcome the 'Thucydides Trap'
sourceOnlyStories.stance: 国际资本与华尔街视角
sourceOnlyStories.source: CNBC Markets (CNBC 市场官方英文)
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: In May, Chinese President Xi Jinping asked U.S. President Donald Trump whether the countries could avoid destructive rivalry. Now, it seems, he thinks they can
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
BEIJING — China is embracing the idea of competition without confrontation, by invoking an academic concept.

"The Thucydides Trap can be overcome," Chinese President Xi Jinping said on arriving at the White House to meet U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday, according to the Chinese side's official readout.

That framing contrasts with the rhetorical question he posed at the May summit of whether the two countries could avoid the Thucydides Trap.

The Thucydides Trap, popularized by Harvard professor Graham Allison in the early 2010s, refers to how tensions between a rising and ruling power have historically often resulted in a war.

Thucydides was an Athenian general in ancient Greece. His historical record of the Peloponnesian War described how Athens' rapid rise in power alarmed Sparta and made war between the two city-states inevitable.

Allison has met Xi and visited China multiple times, including in June 2026 for a World Economic Forum event. Allison was founding dean of Harvard's Kennedy School, which for decades trained many of China's government officials.

The academic previously worked in the U.S. government as Assistant Secretary of Defense under President Bill Clinton in the 1990s and Special Advisor to the Secretary of Defense under President Ronald Reagan in the 1980s.

Xi referred to the Thucydides Trap during a rare interview published by HuffPost in 2014.

"We all need to work together to avoid the Thucydides Trap — destructive tensions between an emerging power and established powers, or between established powers themselves," Xi said.

The Chinese leader's state visit to the U.S. this week was his first in 11 years. A state media article following his 2015 visit noted Xi's interest in the Thucydides Trap reflected his view that it's major powers' suspicion of each other, rather than any sense of inevitability, that results in the conflict that the term predicted.

Xi's comment on Thursday about overcoming the Thucydides Trap followed remarks on peaceful coexistence — that the U.S. and China can have "healthy" competition without confrontation.

"It should be a race of catching up with one another, not a wrestle in which one either wins or loses," Xi said, adding the two countries' militaries should improve crisis communication and prevention.

This establishment of a bottom line — competing intensely without military conflict — is the "most significant political outcome" of the summit, Cui Shoujun, a professor at Renmin University of China's School of International Studies, said in Chinese, translated by CNBC. "This injected certainty into the volatile bilateral relationship."

Trump's comments on Xi's arrival at the White House only emphasized general collaboration.

The U.S. president has yet to comment on Taiwan around this summit, despite Xi calling on the U.S. to "oppose 'Taiwan independence,'" according to Beijing's readout of the two presidents' talks on Thursday.

—CNBC's Anniek Bao contributed to this report.

position.narrativeFocus: 聚焦中国最高领导人在白宫会晤中提出“修昔底德陷阱是可以跨越的”这一核心叙事，梳理该学术概念的历史沿革与中方立场演变，解读中方借此传递“良性竞争、避免军事对抗”的战略底线，同时对比美方仅强调普遍合作与对涉台等敏感议题的沉默态度。

consensus: 中美两国领导人在白宫举行了会谈，这是中国领导人11年来的首次对美对等国事访问。
双方均认可大国之间需要沟通与避免不可控冲突，需开展某种形式的合作与互动。
“修昔底德陷阱”概念源自大国守成与崛起引发冲突的历史规律，由格雷厄姆·艾利森普及，且在双边外交叙事中被频繁讨论。
disagreements: 战略定位与表态侧重点存在温差：中方系统性阐释“竞争而不对抗、跨越修昔底德陷阱”的框架，强调两军危机预防与健康竞争；美方领导人公开表态则偏向概括性的“普遍合作”，未全面背书该理论框架。
台湾问题立场与表态不对称：中方在官方通报中明确呼吁美方“反对‘台独’”，而美方总统在本次峰会期间并未就台湾问题作出公开置评。
成果定性认知差异：中国学者认为确立“激烈竞争但不冲突”的底线是峰会最重要的政治成果，但美方官方未对此予以对等高度的确认或制度化背书。
blindSpots: 缺乏美方对“修昔底德陷阱”叙事的官方直接回应或反驳细节，难以判断美方决策层是否认同“良性竞争”的界定。
未展开报道经贸、关税、科技限制等具体结构性矛盾在本次峰会中是否有实质性让步或谈判进展。
对两军如何具体落实“危机沟通与防范”缺乏操作层面的细节与机制化信息。

Files could have seismic consequences for online casinos, including those accused of illegally targeting consumers

The secrets of thousands of online casinos have been laid bare in a vast leak of data that could have seismic consequences for offshore gambling firms, including some accused of illegally targeting consumers around the world.

The Casino Secrets leak reveals tens of thousands of previously confidential files stored by the gambling regulator on the Caribbean island of Curaçao.

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: A 'library' of bacteria-killing viruses: Harnessing the power of phages
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: An estimated 38 trillion bacteria live in the human body—and only a small fraction are harmful to our health. However, the harmful ones can cause serious illness, especially when they develop resistance to antibiotics.
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
by University of Colorado School of Medicine

edited by Sadie Harley, reviewed by Andrew Zinin

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies. Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

An estimated 38 trillion bacteria live in the human body—and only a small fraction are harmful to our health. However, the harmful ones can cause serious illness, especially when they develop resistance to antibiotics.

To overcome drug resistance and fight severe, hard-to-treat infections, researchers are turning to a type of virus found in nature that infects only bacteria: bacteriophages, or "phages" for short.

A team of University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine researchers has spent the last 15 years compiling a library of phages to target especially stubborn bacteria that naturally live in the intestines.

"Phages have been used historically for decades as tools to understand molecular biology, but there's been a resurgence in interest in them due to the rising incidence of antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections," says Breck Duerkop, Ph.D., associate professor in the Department of Immunology & Microbiology. "We can isolate viruses against infections that are difficult to treat, and some of the viruses will kill the bacteria very readily."

Just like human cells, bacterial cells can be infected by viruses. Duerkop says nearly all bacteria have viruses that infect them, so phages are found in practically any environment where bacteria live. Viruses generally aren't considered living things, but they contain genetic material (DNA or RNA), and they can use host cells to make copies of themselves.

In human cells, according to the National Human Genome Research Institute, a virus gets inside a host cell by binding to a receptor on the cell surface, much like a key unlocking a door. Once inside, DNA or RNA from virus particles takes over cellular functioning and uses materials in the cell to create more virus particles, which can then infect other cells. Viruses disrupt cell activity and damage their host cells, sometimes killing them.

Phages can poke holes through cell walls and inject genetic material directly into bacterial cells. Importantly, phages can't infect human cells, but they can cause similar damage inside bacterial cells as other viruses do in human cells.

Duerkop's research group finds and isolates phages to study how they kill bacteria, how bacteria may become resistant to them, and how the phages can be combined with FDA-approved drugs to treat people with serious bacterial infections.

These researchers are especially interested in treatment-resistant bacteria. They primarily study Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium, two highly drug-resistant bacterial species that normally live in the human gut without causing problems but can cause severe infections, especially in people with compromised immunity.

Other antibiotic-resistant bacteria, including emerging pathogens like Enterobacter hormaechei and Klebsiella oxytoca, have also piqued the team's interest.

To find the right phages, the team gathers viruses from untreated wastewater, which contains these and other types of bacteria that make up the gut microbiome. After exposing the bacteria they're trying to target to the wastewater, the researchers grow the bacteria on agar plates (known as bacterial lawns). They wait a little while, then extract phages directly from the round plaques that form within the bacterial lawns.

From there, the team uses a centrifuge to purify the phage samples and stores the phages in buffers in the refrigerator, where they are stable and have long shelf lives.

Duerkop says he aims to keep a variety of phages on hand that can infect the bacteria his team is interested in. His team currently has more than 30 different viruses that infect enterococcal bacteria and roughly 15 to 20 that infect Enterobacter and Klebsiella.

"The idea of generating a library is you want some diversity," says Duerkop. "Not every phage infects every type of bacteria. They're very specific." Phages can broadly infect strains of a particular bacterial species or be specific to a single strain, making them very precise.

Phages have shown promise as a treatment for these types of infections. They can be combined with standard antibiotics and delivered orally or directly into the bloodstream via an IV, especially if the patient has a blood infection (septicemia). Phages have even been used topically to treat infected burns and other skin injuries.

Phages aren't a cure-all, and bacteria can develop resistance to the phages themselves, but they can be an effective option when traditional antibiotics aren't working on their own. Duerkop says antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections aren't going away anytime soon, so it's essential to continue researching what phages can do.

"It's imperative that we explore creative ways to use phages in combination with antibiotics to target antibiotic-resistant bacteria," says Duerkop.

"We are just beginning to scratch the surface on the diversity of phages that have therapeutic potential. By continuing to study the biology of these phages, we stand to learn more about our natural world and the role of phages in it."

Provided by University of Colorado School of Medicine

科罗拉多大学安舒茨医学院的研究团队在过去15年中构建了一个针对肠道难治细菌的噬菌体库。
噬菌体是一种仅感染细菌的自然病毒，不能感染人体细胞。
Duerkop的研究团队主要研究粪肠球菌（Enterococcus faecalis）和屎肠球菌（Enterococcus faecium），并关注霍氏肠杆菌（Enterobacter hormaechei）与产酸克雷伯氏菌（Klebsiella oxytoca）。

Duerkop团队目前拥有超过30种感染肠球菌的病毒，以及约15到20种感染肠杆菌和克雷伯氏菌的病毒。
噬菌体可与标准抗生素联合使用，可通过口服、静脉注射（IV）或局部外用给药。
细菌也可能对噬菌体本身产生耐药性，噬菌体并非万灵药。

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: We're gonna need a lot more mathematicians
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
[This is a guest post by Amit Sahai. This blog post was initially written in a different file format and converted using AI. — T.]

When I was an undergraduate student, I remember talking with several students who felt that the pace at which the top students could understand new math concepts was far too fast for them. They, too, could understand the ideas, but it would take them much longer. Eventually, almost all of these students gave up their dream of pursuing research mathematics and found something else to do. I have been thinking about those students a lot in the last few days.

The research mathematics community consists largely of those of us who either rarely felt that way, or who felt it and managed to overcome it through hard work. We have had the good fortune to find a place in mathematics where we could make progress. But we are now entering a time for humility: a time when all of us are going to know what it feels like to be unable to keep up.

The AI systems I have worked with are already producing beautiful new ideas. They are doing far more than impressive calculations or quickly carrying out arguments that a strong human researcher would already understand. And we probably can’t even imagine the wonderful ideas that future systems will be capable of producing.

When we feel that we cannot keep up, will we take that as a reason to leave research mathematics, like the students I am remembering? As more of us experience this, there will undoubtedly be a temptation to draw the same conclusion as they did: If the machines can move so much faster than us, perhaps we should find something else to do.

For our community to give up the work of understanding would be a profound abdication of our responsibility to humanity. Each of us is entitled to choose a different life. The responsibility I am talking about belongs to us collectively: to build a future in which humans can understand and contribute to the discoveries that will change our world. A future with meaningful human agency.

Struggle is essential to understanding difficult concepts. Fortunately, this struggle can be shared. I have been blessed to experience this time and time again with my students and collaborators. Imagine a multitude of research groups, each with sustained support, each spending a term or a year trying to understand an extraordinary set of ideas produced by an AI system, with the help of AI systems. [1]

This may very well be among the most important mathematical work in the years to come, and we should support and prioritize it accordingly. This enterprise will require a significant expansion in the number of mathematically sophisticated human researchers available world-wide, as major breakthrough ideas accumulate.

Why should society want this? So far, this might sound like a utopian fantasy for us – a civilization focused on depth of human understanding, awash with mathematicians and physicists and the like. I would certainly love to live in such a world. And indeed there are deep philosophical reasons for society to move in this direction. But I think society has a much more immediate stake in making this possible, too.

Imagine that a future AI system proposes a radically new design for a one terawatt nuclear fusion power plant. It has found a way to sustain and control fusion that no human had conceived of. The design promises abundant, inexpensive, clean electricity. Robots stand ready to manufacture the components and build the plant.

A terawatt is an insane amount of electrical power. We would be deciding whether to construct a machine that handles extraordinary flows of energy using principles we have never conceived of, let alone put into practice. We would need to understand how failures can be contained, what happens to energy already stored in the system when it shuts down, how we can be sure that the materials that make up the power plant behave as expected, and what other questions we should ask before proceeding. The very novelty that makes the proposal exciting would mean that we cannot inherit confidence from decades of operating similar plants or experiments.

Before approving construction, I would want communities of humans to understand why the design works and what justifies confidence in its safety. I would hope that we all would.

Human involvement does not automatically improve a technical decision , and I see no reason to insist that humans manually repeat work an AI system might be able to perform more reliably, even including proving mathematical guarantees. But a theorem can only exist within a model. Understanding the guarantee means understanding the model, the experimental evidence for it, and our uncertainties about the accuracy of the model. This is demanding work, and mathematically sophisticated people must be available to engage with it.

One might respond that AI systems should handle those questions too, and ultimately decide whether the plant should be built. That is a serious position. But it asks us to accept a future in which decisions of enormous consequence rest on reasons that no human community understands.

I do not want us to arrive at that future simply because we failed to invest in our own capacity to understand. Human agency is a value of fundamental importance. We must retain the ability to meaningfully consider alternatives and decide what kind of world we want to be a part of building. I think it is worth the effort. [2]

To take on this responsibility, we may need to broaden our view of what a mathematician can contribute. I have in mind something like a “deployable intellectual reserve”: communities of mathematically sophisticated people that humanity can call upon to help understand consequential AI-enabled breakthroughs.

Our ability to understand difficult and unfamiliar ideas may become one of the most important contributions we can offer to society. We should be willing to bring that skill to problems far beyond our usual research interests. [3] Doing so asks us to expand our sense of our vocation.

A counter-argument might be that AI systems will make each of us so much more effective that fewer people could do this work, even as the pace of discovery accelerates. But each of us is merely human. We have fundamental limitations based on our biology. Depth of understanding needs time and a pace of life that humans can sustain. Each individual human can only be asked to do so much, but through earnest cooperation we can accomplish much more.

If AI fulfills its promise, we will encounter more beautiful and consequential ideas than we have ever seen. We must respond by building thriving human communities that can understand them together.

We’re gonna need a lot more mathematicians.

The ideas and opinions presented here are entirely my own, but GPT 6 Astra was instrumental in helping me draft this note. I also thank my former student Dakshita Khurana, my current student Isaac Hair, my colleague Terence Tao, and my family members Anant Sahai and Gireeja Ranade for valuable feedback. Note that there is much more to be said here, but I tried to keep this relatively short to focus succinctly on my primary thoughts.

[1] By this, I do not mean to imply that only AI-created results will be of interest in the future. But for major results generated by humans, we already have a tradition of spending extended periods of time studying them.

[2] And the relevant understanding cannot belong only to the organization proposing the technology. Imagine a public hearing at which the company’s experts are the only people capable of following the technical argument. Independent expertise is critical.

[3] Indeed, AI systems are likely to be very helpful in allowing researchers with diverse backgrounds to talk effectively with one another, and more generally understand unfamiliar concepts.

position.narrativeFocus: 呼吁在 AI 驱动发现的时代大幅增加数学家储备。核心叙事在于：AI 正在产生超出单个人类直觉的新思想，人类不应因无法跟上节奏而放弃研究，而应组建由精通数学的研究人员构成的“可部署智力储备”，以深入理解和审验 AI 提出的突破性方案（如高风险的核聚变电厂设计），从而在重大科技决策中捍卫人类能动性与独立验证权。
stakeholders: 数学与理论计算机科学研究界
AI 系统研发团队及科技企业

未来可能受 AI 极端技术方案（如能源基建）直接影响的公众
consensus: AI 系统在产生复杂、非常规创意及进行高级推理/计算方面的能力正迅速增强
人类个体的生物学认知速度存在物理局限，单靠个人难以跟上 AI 的爆发式产出
理解复杂 AI 发现并确保技术安全需要人类跨学科的合作与严谨审查
disagreements: 人员需求规模：作者认为随着 AI 突破累积，需要大幅增加数学家数量；反方观点则认为 AI 工具的大幅增效意味着更少的研究人员即可完成相应工作
技术治理模式：作者坚持重大工程与科学决策必须由具备理解能力的人类社区验证；替代观点认为可以直接将验证与决策责任交由更强大的 AI 自主闭环处理
数学家的职业定位：传统纯数学研究主要关注人类自主提出的抽象理论，而作者呼吁将数学家角色拓展为协助社会理解 AI 复杂突破的“智力储备”
blindSpots: 未探讨扩招并长期资助庞大“数学智力储备”所必需的现实经济机制、科研经费分配及制度可行性
预设了精通数学的人类群体在面对极其高维或非人类概念体系的 AI 理论时必然具备“完全理解”的可行性，未深入探讨存在不可解释性认知识差的可能

sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
New research suggests the technology could be used to increase out-of-hospital access to life-saving devices

Drones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people experiencing cardiac arrests when not in hospital, researchers have suggested.

In the UK alone, there are more than 30,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests a year where emergency medical services attempt to resuscitate the individual, according to the British Heart Foundation. However, fewer than one in 10 people survive such an event, and some who do are left with neurological problems.

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: Climate crisis is affecting children's nutrition
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: Wildfires, floods and other extreme weather events are no longer the only ways climate change affects children around the world. Increasingly, it also affects their diets. Droughts reduce agricultural production, floods cut off roads and disrupt supply chains, and rising prices limit families' access to fruits, vegetables and other fresh foods.
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
by Marina Maintinguer Norde, Aline Martins de Carvalho, Fernanda Gomes Ferreira Teixeira, Mariana Ceci, The Conversation

edited by Swati Mestri, reviewed by Andrew Zinin

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies. Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

peer-reviewed publication

written by researcher(s)

Wildfires, floods and other extreme weather events are no longer the only ways climate change affects children around the world. Increasingly, it also affects their diets. Droughts reduce agricultural production, floods cut off roads and disrupt supply chains, and rising prices limit families' access to fruits, vegetables and other fresh foods.

In this scenario, cheaper, longer-lasting products with low nutritional value are gaining ground, increasing the risk of two conditions that, at first glance, may seem contradictory: childhood obesity and malnutrition.

The Interactive Panel on Global Syndemic in Children Under 5 seeks to highlight these relationships. The dashboard is part of the project Global Syndemic: The Impact of Anthropogenic Climate Change on the Health and Nutrition of Children Under Five Served by the Unified Health System (SUS). It presents Brazilian municipal-level data on nutritional issues and greenhouse gas emissions.

The dashboard aims not only to show where malnutrition and overweight are concentrated in the country but also to help users understand how these conditions are distributed and how they relate to environmental factors. Users can set severity alerts when more than one health issue is present in the same municipality or when conditions show a worsening trend over the years.

The tool was developed by Sustentarea, a research group that brings together Brazilian researchers, students and professionals from different fields to study and develop creative interventions related to food systems, sustainable nutrition and the global syndemic. The research and outreach group is based at the School of Public Health of the University of São Paulo (FSP-USP).

The starting point for understanding this issue is that obesity, malnutrition and climate change are not isolated problems. In 2019, an international commission writing in the scientific journal The Lancet brought these three crises together under the concept of global syndemic.

The term "syndemic" describes the simultaneous occurrence of two or more epidemics that interact, exacerbate each other's effects and share common social causes. In the case of the global syndemic, obesity, malnutrition and climate change coexist and are driven by similar structural factors. These include social inequality, limited access to healthy foods and sustainable food production systems. Transportation and changes in land use also contribute, with impacts on human health and the environment.

At the heart of these dynamics are food systems, which encompass the people and organizations involved in food production, processing, distribution, marketing and consumption, as well as the interactions among them and external influences such as environmental, economic, political, technological and cultural factors.

These systems are associated with approximately 74% of Brazil's greenhouse gas emissions. At the same time, they determine which foods reach different regions, how much they cost and who can afford them—a situation that can contribute to both malnutrition and overweight.

The panel focuses on children under 5, who are in a phase of high biological and social vulnerability. In the early years, diet and environmental conditions influence growth, development, immunity and health throughout life.

The effects of the climate crisis and malnutrition are not distributed equally: young children and low-income families tend to suffer more severe impacts and have fewer resources to adapt.

The tool compiles data for Brazilian municipalities from 2008 to 2019 and allows users to track trends in stunting and overweight alongside per capita greenhouse gas emissions. Rather than addressing each problem separately, it seeks to identify where they overlap and which areas should be prioritized in health, food and climate policies.

To identify the most vulnerable municipalities, the dashboard combines data on stunting and overweight from the Brazilian Ministry of Health's Food and Nutrition Surveillance System (Sisvan) with municipal estimates of greenhouse gas emissions from SEEG Brasil.

The analysis considers both the situation recorded in 2019 and the trends in these indicators from 2008 to 2019. The years 2020–2022 were excluded because they represent an atypical period. During the COVID-19 pandemic, demand for medical care fell, significantly distorting the trends used in the analysis and compromising the reliability of the data for that period.

Each municipality receives a rating ranging from "very good" to "very poor" for each of the syndemic's three components, based on whether the indicator increased or decreased and its level in the last year analyzed. The nutritional criteria follow guidelines from UNICEF, the World Health Organization and the World Bank, while the emissions limits were defined based on climate targets set by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).

The results are then combined. The panel also identifies areas with a double burden of malnutrition—where undernutrition and overweight coexist—and those where nutritional problems are associated with high emissions. The remaining categories indicate specific alerts for climate, undernutrition or overweight, as well as more favorable situations.

This does not mean, however, that a municipality's emissions directly cause the nutritional problems observed there. The maps serve primarily to identify geographic patterns, guide new research and help policymakers direct health, food and climate policies.

There is no single Brazilian food system. Conditions related to production, access, consumption and environmental impact vary according to the economic, social and geographic characteristics of each region.

To represent this diversity, the researchers used the Brazilian Multidimensional Index of Sustainable Food Systems (MISFS-R). The index comprises 46 indicators organized into four dimensions—social, nutritional, environmental and economic—and allows for a comparison of the performance of the states and their capitals. By grouping places with similar characteristics, the researchers identified four major food system profiles in Brazil:

1) Agricultural Belt—comprising the Brazilian states of Acre, Rondônia, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Goiás and Tocantins. It is characterized by strong agricultural and livestock production and indicators of sound economic development, but also by high environmental pressure associated with extensive livestock farming and deforestation.

2) Central Economic Hub—comprising Brazilian states in the South and Southeast regions. It shows the best overall performance on the index. Nevertheless, it faces challenges such as gender and racial inequalities in rural areas and high pesticide use.

3) Latent Development Axis—corresponding to the Brazilian states of the Northeast region. It has the most unfavorable results in terms of income, food productivity and nutrition indicators.

4) Vulnerability Frontier—comprising the Brazilian states of Pará, Amazonas, Roraima and Amapá. This area is marked by a higher prevalence of food insecurity, lower dietary diversity and difficulties in accessing food.

These four profiles help put the panel's data in context. In one region, food-related problems may be linked to low income and limited access. In another, they may stem from the expansion of food environments dominated by ultra-processed products or from the environmental consequences of an intensive production model.

The panel's analysis reinforces that protecting children's health requires action beyond the health sector. Ensuring adequate nutrition in early childhood depends on policies related to income, food security, sustainable food production, food supply, school meal programs, environmental protection and adaptation to climate change.

By linking climate, nutrition and children's health, the panel shows that addressing malnutrition and obesity also means addressing the social and environmental conditions that cause them.

Journal information: The Lancet

Provided by The Conversation

keyTakeaways: 气候变化通过极端天气破坏农业生产和供应链，导致价格上涨，促使家庭转向廉价且营养价值低的食品，进而增加儿童肥胖与营养不良并存的风险。
2019年，《柳叶刀》（The Lancet）杂志发表的一项国际委员会报告将肥胖、营养不良和气候变化三大危机归入“全球流行病协同/协同流行”（global syndemic）概念之下。
来源叙事重点：介绍圣保罗大学公共卫生学院开发的互动分析面板，将儿童早期营养不良、肥胖与气候变化结合在“全球协同流行”（Global Syndemic）框架下，探讨巴西食物系统多维特征及环境-健康政策协同治理的紧迫性。

facts.claim: 气候变化通过极端天气破坏农业生产和供应链，导致价格上涨，促使家庭转向廉价且营养价值低的食品，进而增加儿童肥胖与营养不良并存的风险。

圣保罗大学公共卫生学院（FSP-USP）的研究团队Sustentarea开发了“5岁以下儿童全球协同流行互动面板”，呈现巴西市政层面的儿童营养与温室气体排放数据。
巴西的食物系统排放量约占该国温室气体排放总量的74%。
该分析仪表板整合了2008至2019年巴西各市的数据，排除了2020至2022年期间的数据，原因在于COVID-19大流行期间就医需求下降扰乱了趋势指标的可靠性。
该工具的数据源包含巴西卫生部食品和营养监测系统（Sisvan）的发育迟缓与超重数据，以及SEEG Brasil的市政温室气体排放估算数据。

市政层面的高温室气体排放并不直接等同于导致当地观察到的儿童营养不良问题，地图主要用于识别地理模式和指导政策。

巴西圣保罗大学公共卫生学院（FSP-USP / Sustentarea研究团队）
巴西统一卫生系统（SUS）与巴西卫生部（Sisvan监测系统）

公共卫生、农业与气候环境政策制定者
国际公共卫生与气候评估机构（WHO、UNICEF、世界银行、IPCC）
consensus: 气候变化正通过极端天气扰乱粮食供应链和提高食品价格，加剧不健康饮食依赖，导致儿童营养不良与肥胖双重负担加剧。
营养问题与气候变化不是割裂孤立的，二者通过食物系统产生深度交织，构成共享社会根源的“协同流行”。
低收入家庭和5岁以下弱势儿童是气候危机与营养危机的首要受害者，适应能力最弱。
单纯依靠卫生部门无法解决早期儿童健康危机，需结合收入、农业生产模式、供餐计划与气候适应进行跨领域系统性干预。
disagreements: 特定市政区的高排放量与该地儿童营养问题之间是否存在直接因果关系（研究明确强调地图反映的是空间重叠与相关性地理模式，而非直接因果机制）。
巴西不同地域食物系统的核心矛盾存在显著分异：农业带面临粗放型畜牧与毁林压力，经济中心面临农药与不平等问题，而东北部及亚马逊脆弱边缘则主要受限于贫困与粮食获取难度。
blindSpots: 研究排除了2020至2022年COVID-19大流行期间的关键数据，无法呈现后疫情时期全球通胀和经济冲击对儿童营养现状的最新动态影响。
缺乏农业与食品工业利益集团在推动超加工食品普及、维持高碳排集约农业方面的经济政治阻力分析，未探讨商业利益游说对跨部门政策落地的制约。
缺少应对具体区域食物系统转型所需的财政成本测算与具体补偿机制建议。

worldStories.title: 日本11岁电竞神童栗原悠希斩获亚运会金牌
worldStories.originalTitle: Yuki Kurihara, Japan’s 11-year-old e-sports prodigy, wins Asian Games gold
worldStories.source: Al Jazeera (半岛电视台官方英文)
worldStories.snippet: Gold medallist Yuki Kurihara, a primary school student, is youngest athlete in host country Japan's Asian Games history.
worldStories.fullContent:
Gold medallist Yuki Kurihara, a primary school student, is the youngest athlete in host country Japan’s Asian Games history.

Japan’s 11-year-old e-sports prodigy Yuki Kurihara said he was “embarrassed” after winning Asian Games gold on Saturday by thrashing a series of opponents up to three times his age.

The bespectacled primary school student, believed to be the youngest competitor at the games in Aichi-Nagoya, won the Puyo Puyo Champions final 10-2.

He is the youngest athlete in the host country Japan’s Asian Games history.

Puyo Puyo Champions is a puzzle game where players try to clear their screen of coloured blobs by lining them up and popping them.

Looking unruffled throughout, Kurihara waltzed into the gold medal match with a string of dazzling displays.

He crushed Thailand’s Tanarak Wongkitkun – a relative veteran at 28 – 10-1 in the semifinals to ensure at least a silver medal.

He did not even smile after beating South Korea’s 24-year-old Kang Dongshin in the final, having gone down 1-0 early on.

“To be completely honest, I felt a bit embarrassed, so I couldn’t really show my expressions or change my face much,” he explained.

Standing on the podium, he bowed slightly as he received his gold medal and gave a small wave to the arena.

“I’m really happy. The gold medal is really beautiful, shiny and heavy,” he said.

“Also, the plush toy is super cute, and it’s cool that it is gold-coloured too.”

Kurihara started playing Puyo Puyo in his first year of primary school and soon started competing and winning in tournaments. He obtained his pro licence in April this year and regularly beats adults.

“It’s hard having to balance it with school and cram school, but it’s really fun,” he said ahead of the games.

There are no publicly available records of the youngest medallists in the history of the Asian Games, which were first contested in 1951.

But Indonesia’s Bunga Nyimas won bronze in women’s skateboarding aged 12 in Jakarta in 2018.

Cui Chenxi, 13, won games gold when she triumphed in the women’s street skateboarding event three years ago in Hangzhou.
worldStories.fullTranslation:
金牌得主栗原悠希（Yuki Kurihara）是一名小学生，也是东道主日本队亚运会历史上最年轻的运动员。

周六，日本11岁电竞神童栗原悠希在接连横扫了多位年龄最高达到他三倍的对手并夺得亚运会金牌后，表示自己感到“有些不好意思”。

这位戴着眼镜的小学生据信是爱知·名古屋亚运会上年龄最小的参赛选手，他在《魔法气泡 冠军》（Puyo Puyo Champions）决赛中以 10-2 的比分强势获胜。

他是东道主日本队亚运会历史上最年轻的运动员。

《魔法气泡 冠军》是一款益智益智消除类游戏，玩家需要通过将彩色泡泡连线消除来清空自己的屏幕。

栗原在比赛全程表现得泰然自若，凭借一系列令人眼花缭乱的精彩表现轻松晋级金牌争夺战。

他在半决赛中以 10-1 横扫28岁的泰国相对“老将”塔纳拉克·翁吉昆（Tanarak Wongkitkun），提前确保了一枚银牌入账。

在决赛中，栗原尽管在开局以 0-1 落后，但在击败24岁的韩国选手姜东信（Kang Dongshin，音译）后，他甚至连笑容都没有露出来。

“老实说，我当时觉得有点不好意思，所以不太能表现出情绪，脸上的表情也没什么变化，”他解释道。

站在领奖台上，他在领取金牌时微微鞠躬，并向场馆四周轻轻招手。

“我真的很开心。金牌非常漂亮、亮闪闪的，而且沉甸甸的，”他说。

“还有，毛绒玩具也超级可爱，而且它也是金色的，非常酷。”

栗原在小学一年级时开始玩《魔法气泡》，不久便开始参赛并屡屡夺冠。他于今年4月获得了职业选手执照，并且经常在比赛中击败成年人选手。

“在学校功课、补习班和电竞之间保持平衡挺不容易的，但这真的非常有趣，”他在赛前表示。

自1951年首届亚运会举办以来，亚运历史上最年轻奖牌得主并没有公开可查的官方纪录。

但印度尼西亚的布恩加·尼玛斯（Bunga Nyimas）曾于2018年在雅加达以12岁的年龄夺得女子滑板铜牌。

而在三年前的杭州亚运会上，13岁的崔宸曦（Cui Chenxi）在女子街式滑板比赛中夺金。

financeStories.fullContent: Have you ever wanted an electric bike that easily transitions from the drudgery of urban asphalt to adventures in gravel and dirt? That’s what a subclass of so-called “electric SUV” (eSUV) e-bikes claims to do, with their wide, all-terrain tires and front and rear suspension, plus practical accessories like fenders and racks. So, that’s what I set out to test on a new TL Carbon e-bike from Amflow, the DJI offshoot that upended the mountain bike industry a few years ago with its incredibly small and powerful Avinox motors. After a month of testing in the heart of Amsterdam — including a three day bikepacking trip along coastal bicycle superhighways and single-track forest routes — I can confirm what you might already expect: there are compromises. But for €3499 / $3,899 you do get a crossover e-bike that can help you fetch groceries during the week and conquer trails on the weekend. [Product: Amflow TL Carbon eSUV e-bike | https://www.amflowbikes.com/product/amflow-tl-carbon-800wh?vid=242841] I rode my first crossover in 2024 when Cowboy launched its appropriately named Cross. That e-bike, like the vast majority of SUV automobiles, is more at home on pavement than dirt. But it looks burly, which attracts a certain kind of buyer hoping for transference. Today, these eSUVs are more popular than ever. Canyon, for example, makes one. Specialized, too. As does Riese & Müller and now Amflow. The Amflow TL Carbon is built upon the same Avinox drive system that threw the electric mountain bike (eMTB) industry into a tizzy two years ago. The TL Carbon is a bit less powerful, sporty, and springy than the impressive Amflow PX Carbon Pro I tested over the summer, but its eMTB roots are undeniable.  [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4661.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4733.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4754-1.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] I tested the TL Carbon on a bikepacking adventure from Amsterdam to the island of Texel at the tip top of the Netherlands. The 170km trip was about 70 percent asphalt, 20 percent gravel and dirt, and 10 percent rutted, hilly, single-track dedicated to mountain bikers. I was more than a little nervous riding the latter on a 19.2kg (42.3lbs) bike loaded down with an 87kg (190lbs) rider and about 20kg (44lbs) of gear. But Amflow’s compact mid-drive Avinox M2 motor, with its 125Nm of torque and 1100W of max output, flattened long, technical hills that other mountain bikers (not loaded down with gear) had to hike. As an eSUV, the TL Carbon has bonafide off-road credentials. I was also pleased by the range I extracted from the 800Wh battery, despite bikepacking on a very windy weekend. Amflow offers an optional battery extender that adds 480Wh to the total capacity, but I didn’t miss it. I rode in a mix of modes, spending the vast majority of the time in battery-sipping Eco mode, only switching into the adaptive Auto mode when facing a strong headwind, and Trail only when trying to dominate a highly technical or steep single-track. On my longest day, I arrived at my destination with 22 percent charge remaining after riding 82.3km (51.1 miles). That works out to an exceptional 7.58Wh per km (or 12.2Wh per mile) for a bike carrying so much gear. And because the TL Carbon’s battery is removable unlike Amflow’s premium eMTB, it can be easily charged behind a bar, at a cafe, or inside a home. I had no problem finding public chargers along the way, but I’m blessed to live in a country with excellent bicycle infrastructure. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4840.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4861.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4853.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] Still, as an eMTB, the Amflow TL Carbon makes plenty of compromises. The 27.5-inch front wheel is fine in town but it doesn’t roll over roots and rocks as well as 29-inch wheels found on modern mountain bikes (there’s clearance to swap a 29er in if you want). The geometry is also more upright than many would want on a trail, and the suspension travel at the front and rear is relatively short, tuned more for potholes than 1-meter drop-offs (yet it handled those fine). And the things you definitely want on a city bike — like the TL Carbon’s integrated lighting, kickstand, bell, mudguards, front rack, and rear rack — are not designed for quick removal and add considerable weight to the otherwise lightweight (just 2.9kg) carbon-fiber frame. Removing everything to go full eMTB could take up to an hour, and then again to return to city mode. If the Amflow TL Carbon is your only bike then it certainly gets the job done in urban environments. But it’s a little like putting leather seats and a stereo inside a WWII-era jeep and calling it a city car.  In town, the Amflow TL Carbon looks out of place. For one thing, it screams I’m expensive, and the gas shock, Fox branding, and wide knobby tires make it stand out from basic city bikes — not something you want in places where bicycle theft is a problem. I wouldn’t feel comfortable parking it on the street overnight which is otherwise the common thing to do in compact, bicycle cities like Amsterdam. Amflow does equip it with Apple Find My to help locate it. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4913.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4963.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4947.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4942.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4960.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4957.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4992.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4968.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4941.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4787.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4698.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4676.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4672.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4656.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4651.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] The tires on the TL Carbon is where the compromises are most apparent. Amflow selected Maxxis Crossmark II tires which are better suited for trails. The deep tread adds rolling resistance and noise to city commutes and the tires lack advanced anti-puncture features found on tires made for commuting and touring. That makes them more vulnerable to flats caused by glass and construction debris commonly found on city streets. And that knobby tread makes fast cornering on pavement feel squirmy, at least until those nubs are eventually ground off by the asphalt. Likewise, there’s no chain guard on the Amflow TL Carbon. That’s fine for mountain biking but a nuisance in the city where that exposed drivetrain can snag trousers and skirts, or leave them stained with grease when heading out for a night on the town. The dropper seat post is as useful on trails as it is in the city. Droppers are pretty mainstream for mountain bikes these days, and they also make the bike easily shareable with riders of different sizes. But the seatpost and saddle can’t be easily locked when parked making them a target for thieves. The front rack paired with a (bring your own) bungee cord makes fetching errands a snap, and the rear rack can be equipped with an MIK HD-compatible bike seat to carry a kid to daycare. The quick-release Amflow-branded panniers and top bag I took bikepacking also work great for city trips. Just remove the panniers when you arrive at the market, fill them with groceries, snap them back to your bike, and away you go. [Image: Maximum Dutchness. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4815_8c3bbe.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] I really enjoyed my time with the versatile Amflow TL Carbon e-bike. It’s no poseur on the trail where it feels surprisingly agile and powerful even when fully loaded. Its hauling capacity also makes it fine for daily life in the city, if you don’t mind the incongruity of riding a mountain bike around town. The Amflow TL Carbon definitely lives up to the title of “sport utility vehicle,” which is more than I can say for most of its gasoline-powered peers. All photos by Thomas Ricker / The Verge. --- Specifications: * Avinox M2 mid-drive motor: Nominal 110Nm, Peak 125Nm * Screen: Avinox DPC100, 2-inch OLED Control Display * Battery: 800Wh Avinox RS800 Battery (removable and lockable) * Controllers: Avinox Wireless Controller × 2 (one on each side of the handlebar) * Charger: Avinox 4A Charger, 168W Output * Rear shock: FOX FLOAT Rhythm, LSR adjustment, Amflow TL tuned, 190×45mm * Front shock: FOX AWL Sport, 120mm, RAIL 2.0 damper, LSR adjustment, 15×110mm Kabolt, 44mm offset * Cassette: CS-M5243, 10-Speed, 11-43T * Brakes: Tektro TKD173 Hydraulic Disc Brakes, 4-Piston Caliper, Customized for Amflow * Wheels: Amflow HTA-25 Front Wheel (27.5″) * Tires: Maxxis 27.5×2.35 Crossmark II Wire Bead/Clincher/EXO/60TPI * Dropper: Amflow TA, 31.6mm (Adjustable Travel: 0/-10/-20mm) ---

你是否曾想要过一辆能轻松从乏味的城市沥青路面切换到砂石与泥土探险的电动自行车？这正是一类被称为“电动SUV”（eSUV）的电动自行车声称能做到的事情——凭借其宽大的全地形轮胎、前后避震系统，以及挡泥板和货架等实用配件。因此，我决定在Amflow最新推出的TL Carbon电动自行车上亲自测试这一点。Amflow是大疆（DJI）旗下的分支品牌，几年前曾凭借极其小巧且强大的Avinox电机颠覆了山地自行车行业。在阿姆斯特丹市中心进行了一个月的测试后——其中包括一次沿着沿海自行车高速公路和森林单行道林道进行的为期三天的单车旅行（bikepacking）——我可以证实你可能早已预料到的事实：确实存在妥协。但只要花3499欧元/3899美元，你就能拥有一辆跨界电动自行车，既能在工作日帮你买菜拉货，又能在周末征服野外林道。

[产品：Amflow TL Carbon eSUV 电动自行车 | https://www.amflowbikes.com/product/amflow-tl-carbon-800wh?vid=242841]

我第一次骑乘跨界车型是在2024年，当时Cowboy推出了命名恰如其分的Cross。那辆电动自行车就像绝大多数SUV汽车一样，在铺装路面上比在泥地里更自如。但它看起来非常粗犷，吸引了某类希望获得这种心理投射的买家。如今，这类eSUV比以往任何时候都更受欢迎。例如Canyon推出了一款，Specialized也有一款，Riese & Müller同样如此，而现在Amflow也加入了这一行列。Amflow TL Carbon基于两年前让电动山地车（eMTB）行业陷入轰动的同一套Avinox驱动系统打造。TL Carbon相比我夏天测试过的令人印象深刻的Amflow PX Carbon Pro，在动力、运动感和回弹性上稍逊一筹，但其eMTB血统毋庸置疑。

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4661.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4733.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4754-1.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

我骑着TL Carbon进行了一次单车探险旅行，从阿姆斯特丹一路前往荷兰最顶端的特塞尔岛（Texel）。这趟170公里的行程中，约70%是沥青路面，20%是砂石与泥土路面，10%是专门供山地车骑手使用的布满车辙且起伏不平的单行林道。骑着一辆重19.2公斤（42.3磅）的自行车，载着87公斤（190磅）的骑手以及约20公斤（44磅）的装备穿行在后一种路段上，我心里非常紧张。但是，Amflow小巧的中置Avinox M2电机凭借其125牛·米的扭矩和1100瓦的最大输出功率，轻松化解了长距离且具技术难度的陡坡，而其他未载装备的山地车手在这些路段上甚至不得不推车徒步。作为一辆eSUV，TL Carbon拥有货真价实的越野资质。

尽管是在一个多风的周末进行单车旅行，800Wh电池所榨取出的续航表现同样令我感到满意。Amflow提供了一个可选的增程电池，可为总容量增加480Wh，但我并未觉得有此需求。我在多种模式下骑行，绝大部分时间处于低能耗的Eco模式，只在遇到强逆风时切换至自适应Auto模式，而在试图征服高难度或极陡峭的单行道时才开启Trail模式。在行程最长的一天，骑行了82.3公里（51.1英里）之后，我到达目的地时仍剩余22%的电量。对于一辆承载如此多装备的自行车来说，这意味着每公里能耗仅为出色的7.58Wh（或每英里12.2Wh）。而且，与Amflow的高端eMTB不同，TL Carbon的电池是可拆卸的，可以很方便地在酒吧吧台后、咖啡馆内或家里充电。一路上我毫不费力地找到了公共充电桩，不过这也是因为我很幸运地生活在一个自行车基础设施极为完善的国家。

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4840.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4861.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4853.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

不过，作为一辆eMTB，Amflow TL Carbon做出了不少妥协。27.5英寸的前轮在市区骑行尚可，但跨越树根和岩石的能力不如现代山地车常见的29英寸大轮（如果你想换，车架空间是允许换成29寸轮组的）。其车架几何形态也比许多人在林道骑行时所期望的更为直立，前后避震行程相对较短，调校更偏向应对路面坑洼而非1米高的落差坠台（尽管它应付这些落差并无大碍）。此外，城市自行车上不可或缺的配置——例如TL Carbon的集成车灯、脚撑、车铃、挡泥板、前货架和后货架——并未采用快拆设计，给原本轻盈（仅2.9公斤）的碳纤维车架增加了相当可观的重量。要拆下所有配件变成纯粹的eMTB可能需要耗费长达一小时，恢复到城市通勤模式又要再花同样的时间。

如果Amflow TL Carbon是你唯一的自行车，那么它在城市环境中完全能够胜任。但这有点像在二战时期的吉普车里塞进真皮座椅和音响，然后将其称为城市代步车。在市区里，Amflow TL Carbon显得格格不入。首先，它浑身上下都在高调宣扬“我很昂贵”，气压避震器、Fox品牌标识和宽大的颗粒胎让它在普通城市自行车中格外惹眼——这在自行车盗窃猖獗的地方可不是什么好事。在像阿姆斯特丹这样紧凑的自行车城市里，把车停在街上过夜是常态，但我可不敢这么做。不过，Amflow确实为其配备了Apple Find My功能以帮助寻车定位。

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4913.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4963.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4947.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4942.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4960.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4957.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4992.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4968.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4941.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4787.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4698.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4676.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4672.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/uplo

ads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4656.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [图片: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4651.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] 

TL Carbon 的轮胎是妥协最为明显的地方。Amflow 选用了更适合越野林道的 Maxxis Crossmark II 轮胎。较深的花纹增加了城市通勤时的滚阻与胎噪，并且这款轮胎缺乏专门针对通勤和旅行用轮胎所配备的高级防扎防刺特性。这使得它们更容易被城市道路上常见的碎玻璃和建筑杂物刺破。而且那种颗粒凸起的胎面会让在铺装路面上快速过弯时产生晃动打滑的感觉，至少在这些胎齿最终被沥青路面磨平之前都会如此。

同样，Amflow TL Carbon 也没有配备链条罩。这对山地骑行来说无可厚非，但在城市里却是个麻烦事，裸露的传动系统可能会勾挂裤腿和裙子，或者在晚上出门进城时蹭上一腿油污。

升降座管在林道越野和城市骑行中同样实用。如今升降座管在山地车上已相当普及，它们也让不同身材的骑手能轻松共享这辆车。但在停车时，座管和车座很难轻易锁住，使其容易成为小偷的目标。

前车架配上一根（需自备的）弹力绳，能让跑腿取物变得轻而易举，而后车架则可以安装兼容 MIK HD 的儿童安全座椅，用来送孩子去托儿所。我在车友露营（bikepacking）时使用的 Amflow 品牌快拆侧驮包和车顶包，在城市出行中同样表现出色。到了集市直接取下侧驮包，装满杂物杂货，再扣回车上，就能轻松上路。

[图片: 浓郁的荷兰风情。https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4815_8c3bbe.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

我非常享受与功能全能的 Amflow TL Carbon 电动自行车相伴的时光。在林道越野时它绝非花架子，即使在满载状态下也出奇地敏捷且动力强劲。它的载物能力也完全能胜任城市日常生活，只要你不介意骑着一辆山地车在城里转悠所带来的违和感。Amflow TL Carbon 绝对配得上“运动型多功能车（SUV）”的称号，相比大多数燃油车同类，它甚至更有资格承受这一美誉。

所有照片均由 Thomas Ricker / The Verge 拍摄。

---
规格参数：
* Avinox M2 中置电机：额定扭矩 110Nm，峰值扭矩 125Nm
* 屏幕：Avinox DPC100，2英寸 OLED 控制显示屏
* 电池：800Wh Avinox RS800 电池（可拆卸且可上锁）
* 控制器：Avinox 无线控制器 × 2（车把左右各一个）
* 充电器：Avinox 4A 充电器，168W 输出
* 后避震：FOX FLOAT Rhythm，带低速回弹（LSR）调节，Amflow TL 调校，190×45mm
* 前避震：FOX AWL Sport，120mm 行程，RAIL 2.0 阻尼，带低速回弹（LSR）调节，15×110mm Kabolt 桶轴，44mm 偏移量
* 飞轮：CS-M5243，10速，11-43T
* 刹车：Tektro TKD173 油压碟刹，4活塞卡钳，Amflow 定制版
* 轮组：Amflow HTA-25 前轮（27.5英寸）
* 轮胎：Maxxis 27.5×2.35 Crossmark II 钢丝胎/开口胎/EXO防割/60TPI
* 升降座管：Amflow TA，31.6mm（可调行程：0/-10/-20mm）

Amflow TL Carbon 电动自行车的售价为 3499 欧元 / 3899 美元。
来源叙事重点：通过长途跨城与林道越野实测，评估大疆旗下品牌 Amflow 推出的跨界电助力自行车 TL Carbon 在城市通勤与越野穿越双重场景下的实际性能表现与产品折衷权衡。

facts.claim: Amflow 是 DJI（大疆）旗下的衍生品牌（offshoot）。
Amflow TL Carbon 电动自行车的售价为 3499 欧元 / 3899 美元。
Amflow TL Carbon 搭载 Avinox M2 中置电机，峰值扭矩为 125Nm（额定 110Nm），最大输出功率为 1100W。
Amflow TL Carbon 配备可拆卸且可上锁的 800Wh Avinox RS800 电池，并支持加装 480Wh 的可选增程电池。
Amflow TL Carbon 碳纤维车架重量为 2.9kg，整车测试重量为 19.2kg（42.3lbs）。
Amflow TL Carbon 配备 27.5 英寸前轮（具有更换 29 英寸轮组的间隙）、升降座管、Apple Find My 定位支持、一体式车灯、挡泥板、支架、车铃以及前后货架。
作者在荷兰阿姆斯特丹至特塞尔岛（Texel）的 170 公里骑行测试中，单日最长骑行 82.3 公里后剩余 22% 电量，能耗约为每公里 7.58Wh（每英里 12.2Wh）。
车辆配备 Maxxis Crossmark II 越野外胎，且未配备链条罩。

unverified: 该车能否完全胜任重度专业山地越野路线（作者指出其车身几何偏直立，避震行程较短，调校更偏向坑洼路面而非1米落差跳台）。
在城市高风险防盗环境中通过 Apple Find My 找回车辆的实际有效性。

evidence.quote: So, that’s what I set out to test on a new TL Carbon e-bike from Amflow, the DJI offshoot that upended the mountain bike industry a few years ago with its incredibly small and powerful Avinox motors.
But for €3499 / $3,899 you do get a crossover e-bike that can help you fetch groceries during the week and conquer trails on the weekend.
But Amflow’s compact mid-drive Avinox M2 motor, with its 125Nm of torque and 1100W of max output, flattened long, technical hills that other mountain bikers (not loaded down with gear) had to hike.

On my longest day, I arrived at my destination with 22 percent charge remaining after riding 82.3km (51.1 miles). That works out to an exceptional 7.58Wh per km (or 12.2Wh per mile) for a bike carrying so much gear.

And the things you definitely want on a city bike — like the TL Carbon’s integrated lighting, kickstand, bell, mudguards, front rack, and rear rack — are not designed for quick removal and add considerable weight to the otherwise lightweight (just 2.9kg) carbon-fiber frame.

position.sourceRole: 科技媒体消费级硬件评测编辑
position.narrativeFocus: 通过长途跨城与林道越野实测，评估大疆旗下品牌 Amflow 推出的跨界电助力自行车 TL Carbon 在城市通勤与越野穿越双重场景下的实际性能表现与产品折衷权衡。
stakeholders: Amflow及其母公司大疆（DJI）
科技消费评测媒体（The Verge）
城市通勤与轻度越野自行车消费者
竞争品牌（如 Cowboy、Canyon、Specialized、Riese & Müller 等）
零部件供应商（FOX、Maxxis、Tektro）
consensus: Amflow TL Carbon 搭载的 Avinox M2 中置电机具备强劲的动力输出（峰值扭矩 125Nm、最大功率 1100W），在重载爬坡时表现出色。
该车配备 800Wh 可拆卸电池，在长途测试中展现出良好的续航能力与能耗控制（测试中单日 82.3 公里后剩余 22% 电量）。
作为跨界‘eSUV’车型，该车兼具前后货架、升降座管、挡泥板等实用配置，同时具备越野脱困能力。
disagreements: 关于越野与城市场景平衡的取舍：一方面越野胎（Maxxis Crossmark II）和山地避震提供了林道通过性，但在城市沥青路面上带来了滚阻大、胎噪明显、缺乏防刺穿保护以及转弯虚位等问题。
车身配置转换的便捷性：城市实用附件（车灯、货架、挡泥板等）增加了整车重量，且非快拆设计导致在纯越野模式与城市模式之间切换费时费力。
城市停放安全与外观定位：高昂的视觉质感与专业减震/越野套件使其在城市街道停放时容易成为盗窃目标，无链条罩设计也易污染日常服饰。
blindSpots: 测试主要依托于荷兰平整且充电设施完善的自行车基础设施，缺乏在基础设施较差或山地落差更大地区的长期适应性数据。
未深入测试车机智能生态及 Apple Find My 在极端丢车情境下的防盗追回成效与电池长期衰减表现。
缺乏同价位竞品（如 Canyon 或 Specialized 相应跨界车型）在同等复杂路况下的横向数据对比。

financeStories.title: 乌克兰军队正尝试使用Steam Deck远程控制机枪炮塔（2023）
financeStories.originalTitle: Ukraine's army is experimenting with using Steam Decks to remote-control gun turrets (2023)
financeStories.fullContent:
A video showcases Valve's hit handheld being used in a very unexpected way.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Steam Deck is a remarkably powerful piece of hardware, capable of doing all sorts of interesting things. But the Ukrainian military appears to have found one use that I'm pretty sure wasn't anticipated in any of Valve's design meetings: As a controller for a remote gun turret.

Photos of the Steam Deck purportedly being used to control a gun turret first turned up in mid-April, shared by TRO Media, but they looked a little suspect: There was nothing to indicate that the Steam Deck in question was being used as part of the weapon, and not just for a spot of Vampire Survivors during a reload.

More recently, though, video from what appears to be the same event has turned up, and a Steam Deck is clearly being used to control the turret.

The purpose of a remotely-controlled turret is obvious: Get a gun on the front line without exposing the people using it to enemy fire. The auto-translated closed captioning in this separate YouTube video (which also shows the Steam Deck in use as a turret controller, but doesn't have as clear an angle on it) makes that point explicitly: "It removes a person from the line of fire, makes it possible to provide [fire] support without being a priority target and causing enemy fire on ourselves." But why use a Steam Deck for such a thing?

It actually makes a lot of sense, according to Bellingcat researcher Aric Toler, who helped uncover the leak of classified military documents on Discord in April.

"Steam Deck is pretty perfect when you think about it," Toler told PC Gamer. "Totally native OS client, great controller you can use, touch screen, etc.

"It makes perfect sense for Steam Deck to be used, assuming the software is Linux-compatible (unless they went through the godawful process of dual-booting Windows on a Steam Deck)."

There's a practical upside to using Steam Decks in this application too. $399 for a base model Steam Deck isn't cheap, but Toler said that control modules on systems like this can be "insanely expensive," and are also subject to export controls, meaning they can be difficult for officially non-aligned nations to acquire. Steam Deck availability, on the other hand, all comes down to Valve's manufacturing capacity, and because it's an all-in-one solution rather than a controller plugged into a separate, discrete system, there are fewer headaches involved all around.

From the video embedded up top, here's a look at the turret control UI on the Steam Deck:

The turrets, called Shablya—Ukrainian for "saber"—were actually developed some years ago by Ukrainian company Global Dynamics. They're equipped with thermal imaging and a range finder, and can handle a number of different weapons including machine guns and grenade launchers. In 2015, a crowdfunding campaign run through the Ukrainian military and civil crowdfunding site People's Project raised ₴445,000 ($12,000) to fund and maintain 10 Shablya turrets for the Ukrainian military.

According to Ukrainian website Vikna.tv, a batch of Shablya turrets was recently deployed with Ukraine's 68th Jaeger Brigade. The unit recently posted its own video of the turret in use on Facebook.

Ironically, none of the Ukrainian sites that hosted or shared the images made any mention of the presence of a Steam Deck—instead, it was people who saw the videos and recognized the device that brought it to wider attention. Toler speculated that the Ukrainian forces "probably just thought it was a standard control set" and so didn't make a fuss about it.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.
financeStories.fullTranslation:
一段视频展示了Valve旗下的热门掌机正被以一种极乎意料的方式使用。

当您通过我们网站上的链接购买商品时，我们可能会获得联盟佣金。具体机制请参阅此处说明。

Steam Deck是一款性能极其强劲的硬件设备，能够胜任各种有趣的任务。但乌克兰军方似乎发现了它的一种新用途，我很确定这在Valve的任何产品设计会议上都未曾被预料到：充当遥控机枪炮塔的控制器。

据称使用Steam Deck控制机枪炮塔的照片最早于4月中旬由TRO Media发布，但当时这些照片看起来有些令人起疑：没有任何证据表明涉事的Steam Deck被作为武器系统的一部分使用，而非仅仅是在装弹间隙玩上一局《吸血鬼幸存者》（Vampire Survivors）。

然而不久前，疑似记录同一事件的视频被曝光，画面中Steam Deck显然正被用来控制该炮塔。

遥控炮塔的用途显而易见：将武器部署在前线，同时避免操作人员暴露在敌方火力之下。在另一段单独的YouTube视频中（该视频同样展示了被用作炮塔控制器的Steam Deck，但拍摄角度没有那么清晰），自动翻译的字幕明确指出了这一点：“它将人员从交火线撤下，使我们能够在不成为优先目标且不引来敌火攻击自身的情况下提供火力支援。”但为什么偏偏要用Steam Deck来做这件事呢？

据曾在4月协助调查Discord涉密军事文件泄露事件的Bellingcat研究员阿里克·托勒（Aric Toler）表示，这其实非常合情合理。

“仔细想想，Steam Deck几乎是完美的，”托勒对PC Gamer表示，“它有完全原生的操作系统客户端、出色的可用操控部件、触摸屏等。”

“只要相关软件兼容Linux，使用Steam Deck是完全合理的（除非他们费尽周折在Steam Deck上搞了双系统安装Windows）。”

在这一应用场景中使用Steam Deck还有实际的优势。基础款Steam Deck售价399美元虽然不便宜，但托勒表示，此类系统专用的控制模块可能会“极其昂贵”，而且还要受到出口管制，这意味着官方非结盟国家很难采购到。相比之下，Steam Deck的供应情况完全取决于Valve的产能；而且由于它是一个一体化解决方案，而非将控制器插入独立分立的系统中，总体上减少了许多令人头疼的麻烦。

从上方嵌入的视频中，可以一窥Steam Deck上的炮塔控制界面UI：

这款名为“Shablya”（乌克兰语意为“军刀”）的炮塔实际上是由乌克兰公司Global Dynamics在数年前研发的。它们配备了热成像仪和测距仪，可搭载包括机枪和榴弹发射器在内的多种不同武器。2015年，通过乌克兰军民众筹网站People's Project发起的一项众筹活动筹集了44.5万格里夫纳（约合1.2万美元），用于为乌克兰军队资助和维护10座Shablya炮塔。

据乌克兰网站Vikna.tv报道，一批Shablya炮塔最近部署到了乌克兰第68猎兵旅。该部队最近在Facebook上发布了自身使用该炮塔的视频。

颇具讽刺意味的是，发布或分享这些画面的乌克兰网站均未提及Steam Deck的存在——相反，是观看视频并认出该设备的网民将其推向了更广泛的公众视野。托勒推测，乌克兰部队“可能只是以为这是一套标准的控制装置”，因此并没有为此大惊小怪。

Andy自始至终都在PC上玩游戏，最初是在基于磁带的TRS80电脑上玩文字冒险和简陋动作游戏的年轻人。随后，他历经了Sierra Online冒险游戏和Microprose模拟游戏的辉煌时期，运营过本地BBS，自学了组装PC，并对角色扮演游戏、沉浸式模拟游戏和射击游戏产生了长期的热爱。他于2007年开始为The Escapist撰写电子游戏新闻，并在2014年加入历史悠久的PC Gamer团队之前一直设法保住了饭碗。他的报道涵盖行业各个方面，从新游戏发布、补丁说明到法律纠纷、Twitch主播争端、电子竞技以及亨利·卡维尔（Henry Cavill）。大量的亨利·卡维尔。

evidence.quote: The Ukrainian military appears to have found one use that I'm pretty sure wasn't anticipated in any of Valve's design meetings: As a controller for a remote gun turret.

The turrets, called Shablya—Ukrainian for "saber"—were actually developed some years ago by Ukrainian company Global Dynamics. They're equipped with thermal imaging and a range finder, and can handle a number of different weapons including machine guns and grenade launchers.

In 2015, a crowdfunding campaign run through the Ukrainian military and civil crowdfunding site People's Project raised ₴445,000 ($12,000) to fund and maintain 10 Shablya turrets for the Ukrainian military.
According to Ukrainian website Vikna.tv, a batch of Shablya turrets was recently deployed with Ukraine's 68th Jaeger Brigade.

$399 for a base model Steam Deck isn't cheap, but Toler said that control modules on systems like this can be "insanely expensive," and are also subject to export controls, meaning they can be difficult for officially non-aligned nations to acquire.

遥控炮塔的核心设计目标是将操作人员移出直接交火线以减少人员伤亡。

financeStories.fullContent:
APOD: 2026 September 26 –…

Astronomy Picture of the Day

Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

Mirrored Meteor and Milky Way

Explanation: On August 15, this perseid meteor streaked through night skies over the Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos at La Palma, Canary Islands, Spain. The bright and colorful meteor trail was captured next to the central Milky Way, whose dark interstellar dust clouds and luminous starlight reach above the horizon. In the foreground of this tantalizing celestial scene is the 23 meter diameter mirror of the prototype Large-Sized Telescope ( LST-1 ). LST-1 is the first telescope constructed at the northern hemisphere site of the innovative Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory . With 198 hexagonal mirror segments and a large, high-efficiency, pixelized camera, LST-1 is designed to detect extremely brief, atmospheric visible light flashes . Lasting about a billionth of a second, the visible light flashes are triggered by energetic gamma-rays from cosmic sources such as distant active galaxies and gamma-ray bursts. Of course, on that night some individual mirror segments of LST-1 also reflected the atmospheric flash of the bright perseid meteor.

financeStories.title: 日本11岁电竞神童栗原悠希斩获亚运会金牌
financeStories.originalTitle: Yuki Kurihara, Japan’s 11-year-old e-sports prodigy, wins Asian Games gold
financeStories.source: Al Jazeera (半岛电视台官方英文)
financeStories.snippet: Gold medallist Yuki Kurihara, a primary school student, is youngest athlete in host country Japan's Asian Games history.
financeStories.fullContent:
Gold medallist Yuki Kurihara, a primary school student, is the youngest athlete in host country Japan’s Asian Games history.

Japan’s 11-year-old e-sports prodigy Yuki Kurihara said he was “embarrassed” after winning Asian Games gold on Saturday by thrashing a series of opponents up to three times his age.

The bespectacled primary school student, believed to be the youngest competitor at the games in Aichi-Nagoya, won the Puyo Puyo Champions final 10-2.

He is the youngest athlete in the host country Japan’s Asian Games history.

Puyo Puyo Champions is a puzzle game where players try to clear their screen of coloured blobs by lining them up and popping them.

Looking unruffled throughout, Kurihara waltzed into the gold medal match with a string of dazzling displays.

He crushed Thailand’s Tanarak Wongkitkun – a relative veteran at 28 – 10-1 in the semifinals to ensure at least a silver medal.

He did not even smile after beating South Korea’s 24-year-old Kang Dongshin in the final, having gone down 1-0 early on.

“To be completely honest, I felt a bit embarrassed, so I couldn’t really show my expressions or change my face much,” he explained.

Standing on the podium, he bowed slightly as he received his gold medal and gave a small wave to the arena.

“I’m really happy. The gold medal is really beautiful, shiny and heavy,” he said.

“Also, the plush toy is super cute, and it’s cool that it is gold-coloured too.”

Kurihara started playing Puyo Puyo in his first year of primary school and soon started competing and winning in tournaments. He obtained his pro licence in April this year and regularly beats adults.

“It’s hard having to balance it with school and cram school, but it’s really fun,” he said ahead of the games.

There are no publicly available records of the youngest medallists in the history of the Asian Games, which were first contested in 1951.

But Indonesia’s Bunga Nyimas won bronze in women’s skateboarding aged 12 in Jakarta in 2018.

Cui Chenxi, 13, won games gold when she triumphed in the women’s street skateboarding event three years ago in Hangzhou.
financeStories.fullTranslation:
金牌得主栗原悠希（Yuki Kurihara）是一名小学生，也是东道主日本队亚运会历史上最年轻的运动员。

周六，日本11岁电竞神童栗原悠希在接连横扫了多位年龄最高达到他三倍的对手并夺得亚运会金牌后，表示自己感到“有些不好意思”。

这位戴着眼镜的小学生据信是爱知·名古屋亚运会上年龄最小的参赛选手，他在《魔法气泡 冠军》（Puyo Puyo Champions）决赛中以 10-2 的比分强势获胜。

他是东道主日本队亚运会历史上最年轻的运动员。

《魔法气泡 冠军》是一款益智益智消除类游戏，玩家需要通过将彩色泡泡连线消除来清空自己的屏幕。

栗原在比赛全程表现得泰然自若，凭借一系列令人眼花缭乱的精彩表现轻松晋级金牌争夺战。

他在半决赛中以 10-1 横扫28岁的泰国相对“老将”塔纳拉克·翁吉昆（Tanarak Wongkitkun），提前确保了一枚银牌入账。

在决赛中，栗原尽管在开局以 0-1 落后，但在击败24岁的韩国选手姜东信（Kang Dongshin，音译）后，他甚至连笑容都没有露出来。

“老实说，我当时觉得有点不好意思，所以不太能表现出情绪，脸上的表情也没什么变化，”他解释道。

站在领奖台上，他在领取金牌时微微鞠躬，并向场馆四周轻轻招手。

“我真的很开心。金牌非常漂亮、亮闪闪的，而且沉甸甸的，”他说。

“还有，毛绒玩具也超级可爱，而且它也是金色的，非常酷。”

栗原在小学一年级时开始玩《魔法气泡》，不久便开始参赛并屡屡夺冠。他于今年4月获得了职业选手执照，并且经常在比赛中击败成年人选手。

“在学校功课、补习班和电竞之间保持平衡挺不容易的，但这真的非常有趣，”他在赛前表示。

自1951年首届亚运会举办以来，亚运历史上最年轻奖牌得主并没有公开可查的官方纪录。

但印度尼西亚的布恩加·尼玛斯（Bunga Nyimas）曾于2018年在雅加达以12岁的年龄夺得女子滑板铜牌。

而在三年前的杭州亚运会上，13岁的崔宸曦（Cui Chenxi）在女子街式滑板比赛中夺金。
